He signed his first professional contract with Rapid Wien at the age of 16 and made his debut in an Austrian Cup match in October 1999. His league debut followed in 2000. During his time with Rapid Wien, spanning 177 games, he scored 27 goals and helped the team win the Austrian Championship in the 2004–05 season. He was recognized as the Austrian Footballer of the Year in 2003.

In January 2006, Ivanschitz moved to Red Bull Salzburg, and then joined Panathinaikos in August of the same year on a two-year loan, which was later made permanent in 2008. He spent three years in Greece before agreeing to a two-year loan deal with Mainz 05 in July 2009, with an option for a permanent contract. Mainz exercised this option early, securing his services permanently in January 2011. He then transferred to Levante in June 2013, scoring his first La Liga goal in August of that year against Rayo Vallecano. He scored three goals in 29 games during his first season with Levante, including one against Valencia.

Ivanschitz continued his career in Major League Soccer, signing with Seattle Sounders FC in August 2015. His debut was delayed by injury but he eventually made an impact, providing an assist in a match against San Jose Earthquakes. A highlight of his time with Seattle was his contribution to their 2016 MLS Cup victory, successfully converting a penalty in the shootout which ultimately secured the title for the Sounders.

Internationally, Ivanschitz earned 69 caps for Austria, scoring 12 goals, and was part of the Austrian team that participated in Euro 2008. He first appeared for Austria in a friendly match against Greece in 2003.

Beyond football, Ivanschitz comes from a musical family and enjoys playing various instruments. He is also connected to the Burgenland Croat community, and his son, Ilia, is currently a footballer with Red Bull Salzburg. Throughout his career he achieved honours including the Austrian Football Bundesliga title with Rapid Wien in 2005 and the MLS Cup with Seattle Sounders FC in 2016, as well as the individual accolade of Austrian Footballer of the Year in 2003.

title: Tanel Ingi
text:
Tanel Ingi, born on November 26, 1976, is an Estonian actor working primarily in stage and film. He is a long-standing performer at the Ugala theatre in Viljandi, where he has been a member of the company since 1998 and continues to perform. His career began while he was still a student, and he has since taken on roles in a remarkably diverse repertoire of plays, encompassing both classic and contemporary works. 

Ingi’s stage work includes performances in plays by internationally renowned authors such as William Shakespeare, Anton Chekhov, Leo Tolstoy, and Victor Hugo. He’s also performed in adaptations of works by A. A. Milne, Robert Louis Stevenson, Mark Twain, Jules Verne, Tom Stoppard, Friedrich Schiller and Estonian writers like August Gailit and Oskar Luts. This demonstrates a breadth of skill and a comfort across various dramatic styles.

Beyond the theatre, Ingi has built a substantial presence in Estonian film and television. His first film role was in the 1999 drama *Lurjus*, also known as *An Affair of Honour*, directed by Valentin Kuik and featuring Taavi Eelmaa. A particularly recognized role came in 2005 with his portrayal of Tõnu in the television film *August 1991*, directed by Ilmar Raag. This film is a dramatization of the events surrounding the failed Soviet attempt to quell the Singing Revolution, a pivotal moment in Estonia’s fight for independence.

Ingi’s television appearances are numerous and span different genres. He has been seen in the children’s series *Nöbinina*, the crime drama *Kelgukoerad* on Kanal 2, and the TV3 series *Kättemaksukontor*. He also participated in *Riigimehed*, an ETV political satire. More recently, he joined the cast of Kanal 2’s *Pilvene all* in 2015, playing the character of Andres Kroon. In 2017, he took on the role of Aivar in the ETV drama series *Pank*, a ten-part production focusing on the emergence and struggles of a new bank in Estonia during the 1990s. In 2020, he expanded his creative involvement in filmmaking by co-directing the comedy feature film *Asjad, millest me ei räägi* alongside Andrejs Ekis.

Tanel Ingi currently lives in Viljandi with his wife, Kätlin. They also maintain a summer residence located in Koeru Parish, near the village of Preedi in Järva County. His formal training began in 1995 at the Kopli-Tallinn Art School, and he later graduated from the Viljandi Culture Academy in 1999.

title: Ted Mack (politician)
text:
Edward Carrington Mack, born in 1933 and passing away in 2018, was a unique figure in Australian politics, distinguished as the only person to be elected and re-elected as an independent across local, state, and federal levels of government. Often called the “father of the independents,” he deliberately limited his time in office to two terms at both the New South Wales state level and in federal parliament to avoid accumulating a parliamentary pension, demonstrating a principled stance against what he saw as excesses in public office.

Mack’s early life saw him educated at Sydney Boys High School and serving in the RAAF before training as an architect at the University of New South Wales, graduating in 1958. He worked as an architect for many years, specializing in hospitals and public housing, and even held positions overseeing hospital design and construction for the NSW Public Works Department and the NSW Housing Commission. He also served on a committee focused on Aboriginal housing in remote areas.

His political career began in 1974 with election to the North Sydney Municipal Council, where he rose to become mayor in 1980, a position he held until 1983, and again in 1987. As mayor, he implemented open government policies, opening council meetings and files to the public, and established numerous committees to encourage public participation in decision-making. He also focused on diversifying council funding sources, successfully reducing reliance on rates. 

In 1981, Mack unexpectedly won the state seat of North Shore, defeating the Liberal opposition leader Bruce McDonald. He continued this pattern of defying expectations in 1990, capturing the federal seat of North Sydney from the long-serving Liberal MP John Spender. As a federal member, he opposed policies like unilateral tariff removal and privatization, and notably voted against Australian involvement in the Gulf War, citing concerns about oil interests and the origins of the conflict. He also championed citizen-initiated referendums and served on the transport and communications committee. 

True to his principles, Mack retired from federal parliament in 1996 to avoid a pension, a move that influenced the subsequent preselection process for his seat. He remained engaged in public life, serving as a delegate to the Australian Constitutional Convention and actively opposing the proposed republican model. He was recognized as a “National Living Treasure” in 1997. 

Even in his later years, Mack continued to support independent candidates, notably assisting Stephen Ruff in the 2015 North Sydney by-election, criticizing the Liberal party’s preselection process. He was diagnosed with brain cancer in 2016 and succumbed to a stroke in November 2018, leaving behind a legacy of independent thought and commitment to public service. A park in North Sydney was renamed in his honour in 2019.

title: Thirayuth Boonmee
text:
Thirayuth Boonmee, born on January 10, 1950, is a prominent Thai social scientist, public intellectual, and former student activist. He rose to national prominence as a student leader at Chulalongkorn University in 1973, spearheading the National Student Center of Thailand (NSCT) in opposition to the military dictatorship led by Thanom Kittikachorn and Praphas Charusathien. The NSCT organized large-scale public protests, including a ten-day boycott of Japanese products to protest Japanese investment in Thailand, drawing tens of thousands of participants.

In October 1973, Thirayuth was arrested alongside twelve other student activists for sedition after distributing leaflets calling for a new constitution. False rumors of their deaths ignited widespread anti-government demonstrations culminating on October 13th with approximately 400,000 protesters assembling near the Democracy Monument and parliament. The students were subsequently released, and the king agreed to oversee the drafting of a new constitution within a year. Thirayuth also played a part in revealing the involvement of the Internal Security Operations Command in the Ban Na Sai village massacre.

Following the violent crackdown on students at Thammasat University in 1976, Thirayuth, like many others, sought refuge with the Communist Party of Thailand (CPT) in the country's jungles. During this period, he became increasingly critical of the monarchy, publicly stating in 1977 that it was “obsolete and deteriorating” and suggesting its abolition would have no negative consequences. However, after the CPT disbanded in the early 1980s, Thirayuth returned to mainstream Thai intellectual life, retracting his socialist views and disavowing his earlier anti-monarchical statements.

Thirayuth pursued higher education in the Netherlands, earning a degree equivalent to a Master of Arts in Philosophy, Sociology, and Anthropology from the International Institute of Social Studies in The Hague and the University of Nijmegen. He returned to Thailand in 1985 and has since been a long-standing faculty member in the Faculty of Sociology and Anthropology at Thammasat University. Recognized for his influence, he was named one of Thailand’s ten most influential public intellectuals in 1997. 

He served as director of the Sanya Dharmasakti Institute for Democracy at Thammasat University from 2008 and was appointed Professor of Anthropology in 2012. In 2015, he transitioned to Thammasat University's College of Interdisciplinary Studies. Throughout his career, Thirayuth has been a vocal critic of political figures; notably, he coined the term "Thaksinocracy" to describe the rule of Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra between 2001 and 2006.

title: Cierre Wood
text:
Cierre Wood, born February 21, 1991, is a former American football player who ultimately received a life sentence for murder. He built a promising athletic career beginning in high school at Santa Clara High School in Oxnard, California, where as a senior he rushed for 1,632 yards and 20 touchdowns, and was named a USA Today All-American in 2008. He was highly recruited, eventually choosing to play college football at Notre Dame over several other prominent universities. 

At Notre Dame, Wood redshirted his first year in 2009. He became a significant part of the team in 2010, starting the last six games after an injury to the primary running back, gaining 603 rushing yards and three touchdowns. He continued to improve, becoming the starting running back in his junior year and recording 1,102 rushing yards with nine touchdowns. His senior year was marked by a two-game suspension for violating team rules, but he still managed 742 rushing yards in the remaining eleven games. 

Wood decided to enter the 2013 NFL draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility. He went undrafted but was signed by the Houston Texans as a free agent. His time with the Texans was brief, as he was released in October 2013 due to unspecified team rule violations. He subsequently had short stints with the New England Patriots, Baltimore Ravens, Seattle Seahawks, and Buffalo Bills, spending time on practice squads and briefly being promoted to active rosters. He even played Canadian football with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats and Montreal Alouettes before being released in 2018.

However, Wood’s life took a tragic turn. In April 2019, he and his girlfriend, Amy Taylor, were arrested in connection with the death of Taylor’s five-year-old daughter, La’Rayah Davis. The child was found with extensive injuries. Wood was accused of subjecting the child to harsh physical punishments, including forced, extreme exercise. In August 2024, Wood was sentenced to life in prison, with the possibility of parole after over twelve years, after entering an Alford plea to charges of second-degree murder and child abuse.

title: Tracy Somerset, Duchess of Beaufort
text:
Tracy Somerset, Duchess of Beaufort, born Tracy Louise Ward in 1958, is a British duchess with a diverse background as an environmental activist and former actress. She is widely known as Tracy Worcester, a name she used throughout much of her career. She descends from a prominent family; her great-grandfather was the 2nd Earl of Dudley, a Lord Lieutenant of Ireland and Governor-General of Australia who held vast land and industrial holdings. Her father was involved in the family brick business, and she is the sister of actress Rachel Ward.

Tracy Worcester began her career with modeling in Paris, followed by work at Christie’s in London and art galleries in New York. She then pursued acting, training at both the Academy of Live and Recorded Arts and the London Drama School. Her most recognized acting role was as Tessa Robinson in the television series *C.A.T.S. Eyes*, and she also appeared in *Doctor Who* and the film *Dance with a Stranger*. She also played the first Miss Scarlett in the television drama game show *Cluedo*. 

In 1987, she married Henry, Marquess of Worcester (later the 12th Duke of Beaufort), and the wedding was attended by the then Prince and Princess of Wales. They divorced in 2018, shortly after her husband inherited the dukedom. They have three children, including the current Marquess of Worcester. 

Since 1989, Worcester has dedicated herself to environmental activism. She has held trustee and directorial positions with organizations such as Friends of the Earth, The Gaia Foundation, and Farms Not Factories – an organization she founded to promote high-welfare, locally sourced meat. Her activism extends to documentary filmmaking, including *Pig Business*, which exposed the issues with intensive pig farming, and *Is Small Still Beautiful in India* and *The Politics of Happiness in Bhutan*. She actively lobbies governments and corporations, even purchasing shares in companies like Tesco to raise concerns about factory farming practices, and has undertaken undercover investigations of pig farms. 

Beyond food systems, she has been involved in broader political activism, supporting the Referendum Party, Caroline Lucas of the Green Party, and Jeremy Corbyn. She also provided bail sureties for Julian Assange. More recently, she has supported George Galloway. In 2020, she launched Forbidden Fruit and Veg, an organic market garden venture on her Badminton estate, utilizing WWOOF participants for labor and training. She also publishes a monthly newsletter dedicated to her work and causes.

title: Yuyan
text:
Yuyan, born with the courtesy name Yanrui and nickname Xiaoruizi on May 17, 1918, and passing away on January 18, 1999, was a Chinese calligrapher descended from the Manchu Aisin Gioro clan, the imperial family of the Qing dynasty. He was a distant cousin of Puyi, the last Emperor of China, and a central figure in the story of the potential succession to the throne after the dynasty’s fall.

Born in Beijing to Pucheng and Jinggui, Yuyan’s lineage traced back to the Daoguang Emperor through his grandfather, Zailian. In 1936, Puyi summoned Yuyan to his court in Manchukuo, a puppet state established by Japan, where they developed a close relationship – Puyi affectionately called him “Little Rui.” 

Following the collapse of Manchukuo, Yuyan’s life took a dramatic turn. He was arrested by the Soviets in 1945 and imprisoned in the Soviet Far East until 1950, alongside Puyi. After being sent back to China, he was incarcerated in the Fushun War Criminals Management Centre from 1950 to 1957. It was during their imprisonment that Yuyan claimed Puyi designated him as his heir, a claim Puyi himself only alluded to in his autobiography as a consideration. However, a formal succession law established in 1937 had already named Puyi’s brother, Pujie, as the next in line.

Life under the People’s Republic of China was marked by hardship. Released from Fushun, Yuyan worked as a teacher and in a factory, but was repeatedly arrested. He endured hard labour in 1959 near Beijing and again during the Cultural Revolution in 1966, being sent to Shanxi. He wasn’t fully released until 1979, after which he worked as a road sweeper in Beijing.

Despite his difficult circumstances, Yuyan continued to practice calligraphy and poetry. He was later recognized for his skills and appointed as a state consultant for the restoration of the Prince Gong Mansion in 1987. His story gained wider attention with the publication of Tony Scotland’s 1993 book, *The Empty Throne*, which details the British journalist’s search for a potential heir to the Chinese imperial throne, with Yuyan as its primary subject.

Yuyan married twice, first to Magiya Jinglan in 1943, and later to Zhang Yunfang after Jinglan’s death in 1948. He had three sons: Hengzhen, Hengkai, and Hengjun. He also had three grandchildren, Hengxing, Jin Yinghui, and Jin Qitong.

title: Esteban Espíndola
text:
Esteban Ezequiel Espíndola López, born on March 22, 1992, is an Argentine professional footballer who plays as a centre-back. He began his professional career with River Plate, though his opportunities were limited initially, appearing only on the bench twice in the Argentine Primera División. He did make his debut for the club in the 2012–13 Copa Argentina against Estudiantes.

In July 2013, Espíndola was loaned to Atlético de Rafaela, also a Primera División team, but only featured in three league matches during the 2013–14 season. He then moved to Nueva Chicago in Primera B Nacional in 2014, but his time there was brief, as he departed without making a single appearance. A move to Belgrano, another Primera División side, followed in February 2015. He spent three seasons with Belgrano, accumulating twenty appearances across all competitions. 

In August 2017, Espíndola was loaned to San Martín, a Primera B Nacional team. This proved a successful move, as he helped the club achieve promotion to the top division.  He then ventured abroad, joining Olimpia in the Liga Nacional of Honduras in August 2018. He played in fourteen games for Olimpia before leaving in December of the same year by mutually terminating his contract. He returned to Argentina in January 2019, signing with Racing de Córdoba in the Torneo Federal A, but experienced relegation with the team. 

Espíndola subsequently returned to Honduras, joining Marathón, where he found goal-scoring form. He scored his first senior career goal on August 11, 2019, in a 1–1 draw against his former club, Olimpia, and went on to score against Honduras Progreso and Real Sociedad.  In July 2020, he moved again, this time to Costa Rica, signing a one-year contract with Saprissa and being assigned the number five shirt.

Before turning professional, Espíndola represented Argentina at the youth level, playing for both the U15 and U17 teams. He participated in the 2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Nigeria, making three appearances for the U17 squad and even scoring a goal – a penalty kick – during a group stage match against Germany. 

Throughout his career, Espíndola has achieved some team honours. He was part of the River Plate squad that won the U-20 Copa Libertadores in 2012 and later celebrated a Liga FPD Clausura title with Saprissa in 2021.

title: Alf Garland
text:
Alfred Barrett Garland, born on March 19, 1932, and passing away on March 9, 2002, was a prominent figure in both the Australian Army and the Returned and Services League of Australia (RSL). He served as the National President of the RSL from 1988 until 1993, and was known for his direct and often controversial views, which frequently put him at odds with the Keating government of the time.

Garland dedicated 35 years to a career in the Australian Army, demonstrating considerable leadership and skill. A significant early command came in 1965 when he led the 1st Special Air Service squadron during operations against Indonesian forces in Borneo. His service extended to the Vietnam War, where he held the position of second-in-command of the 7th Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment. He also served as Australia’s chief liaison officer to United States forces during the conflict, a role requiring strong diplomatic and operational capabilities. 

Prior to his national role, Garland was President of the RSL branch in the Australian Capital Territory. As National President, he became a public voice on a range of issues, often sparking debate with his strong opinions. Beyond veteran’s affairs, Garland actively engaged in political and social commentary. He was a staunch monarchist, and in 1998, represented New South Wales as a delegate for the Australian Monarchist League at the Australian Constitutional Convention. There, alongside Bruce Ruxton, he vigorously opposed the movement towards Australia becoming a republic. Their consistent opposition to republican arguments, including a deliberate attempt to prolong debate by recounting his family's historical ties to the British Crown, proved disruptive and frustrating to those advocating for a republic. He also held leadership positions within the Australian Monarchist League, serving as chairman for both the NSW and ACT branches.

Garland’s concerns extended to economic and immigration policy. He actively campaigned against the Multifunction Polis (MFP), a technology city project funded by Japan. Furthermore, he publicly expressed concerns about the level of Asian immigration to Australia. In 1988, he advocated for changes to immigration selection policies, stating the need to maintain Australia as a “predominantly European” nation, and famously declaring “We want to retain Australia for Australians.” 

After a prolonged illness, Garland died at the age of 69 from motor neurone disease, leaving behind a legacy as a dedicated military officer and a vocal, sometimes divisive, advocate for his beliefs.

title: Philippe Coutinho
text:
Philippe Coutinho, born in Rio de Janeiro in 1992, is a Brazilian professional footballer currently playing for Vasco da Gama. He’s renowned for his vision, passing ability, dribbling skills, and talent for scoring from long range. Coutinho developed through Vasco da Gama’s youth system and signed with Inter Milan in 2008 at age 16, although he remained on loan with Vasco until he turned 18, becoming a key player during his time there and helping them achieve promotion to the top tier.

He officially joined Inter Milan in 2010, making his debut in the UEFA Super Cup, and later contributing to a crucial Champions League victory against Bayern Munich. Despite scoring a couple of goals for Inter, he struggled for consistent playing time and was loaned to Espanyol in 2012, where he impressed by scoring five goals in 16 appearances. He returned to Inter, but continued to find opportunities limited.

Coutinho’s career took off when he joined Liverpool in January 2013. He quickly became a fan favourite, earning accolades such as being named to the PFA Team of the Year in 2015 and winning Liverpool’s Player of the Year awards in both 2015 and 2016. He established himself as a crucial part of the team, demonstrating impressive skill and playmaking ability. 

In January 2018, he made a high-profile move to Barcelona for a substantial fee. While at Barcelona, he secured two La Liga titles and various domestic trophies. Following a period where he wasn't a regular starter, he was loaned to Bayern Munich for the 2019–20 season, where he was part of the team that achieved a treble win – the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and UEFA Champions League. He then spent a loan spell at Aston Villa, which later became a permanent transfer.

On the international stage, Coutinho made his debut for Brazil in 2010 and has represented his country in several major tournaments, including the Copa América in 2015 and 2016, and the FIFA World Cup in 2018, where he scored two goals. He was also part of the Brazil squad that won the 2019 Copa América.

Coutinho’s early life was spent in Rio de Janeiro, where he was a shy child who discovered his passion for football through his older brothers. Starting with futsal, he honed his skills on the streets before joining a local academy, eventually being scouted by Vasco da Gama. His journey reflects a rise from humble beginnings to becoming a prominent figure in the world of professional football.

title: Jefferson Thomas
text:
Jefferson Thomas was born in Little Rock, Arkansas, in 1942, the youngest of seven children and named after President Thomas Jefferson. He initially attended the segregated Horace Mann High School, where he participated in track and field. In 1957, as a sophomore, he volunteered to be one of the first African-American students to integrate Little Rock Central High School, becoming part of the group known as the Little Rock Nine.

The initial attempts to enter the school on September 4, 1957, were blocked by the Arkansas National Guard, acting under the governor’s orders, and a hostile crowd of approximately 400 people. A larger mob, around 1000 strong, again prevented their entry on September 23rd. President Dwight D. Eisenhower intervened, federalizing the National Guard and deploying federal troops to ensure the students' safety and allow them access to the school. Federal forces remained at Central High for the duration of the school year.

Despite enduring harassment, Thomas successfully graduated from Little Rock Central High School in 1960 and subsequently enrolled at Wayne State University in Detroit. He later moved to Los Angeles, California, in 1961, where he became involved in civil rights activism, serving as Treasurer of the NAACP Youth Council and State President of the Progressive Baptist Youth Convention. He continued his education at Los Angeles State College, becoming President of the Associated Engineers while earning a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration. Thomas also served in the U.S. Army during the Vietnam War as an infantryman in the 9th Infantry Division. 

He later narrated the 1964 United States Information Agency film *Nine from Little Rock*, reflecting on the experience and stating that challenges could lead to improvement. The film, intended to counter negative perceptions of American racial issues during the Cold War, was widely acclaimed and distributed internationally. 

Thomas spent his later years in Columbus, Ohio, with his wife, Mary, and dedicated himself to community service, mentoring youth through the Village to Child Program. He received an Honorary Doctor of Humane Letters from Ohio Dominican University in 2001. He was a frequent speaker across the country, sharing his experiences, and was recognized with numerous awards including the Congressional Gold Medal, presented to the Little Rock Nine by President Bill Clinton in 1999, and the NAACP's Spingarn Award, also in 1999. The state of Arkansas honored the Little Rock Nine with statues on the Capitol grounds in 2005. He retired in 2004 after 27 years as a civil servant with the Defense Finance and Accounting Service. Jefferson Thomas passed away in 2010 from pancreatic cancer, becoming the first member of the Little Rock Nine to die. He was interred in Forest Lawn Memorial Park in Glendale, California.

title: Matthew Perry
text:
Matthew Perry, born in Williamstown, Massachusetts, in 1969, was a celebrated actor recognized internationally for his role as Chandler Bing on the television sitcom *Friends* (1994-2004). He also appeared in *Ally McBeal* and earned Emmy nominations for his work in *The West Wing* and *The Ron Clark Story*. Beyond *Friends*, Perry starred in films like *Fools Rush In*, *Almost Heroes*, *The Whole Nine Yards*, and *17 Again*, and led the NBC series *Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip*. He also co-created, wrote, and starred in the short-lived ABC sitcom *Mr. Sunshine* and later co-developed and starred in a revival of *The Odd Couple*. He had recurring roles in *The Good Wife* and *The Good Fight*, and portrayed Ted Kennedy in *The Kennedys: After Camelot*. His final televised appearance was in *Friends: The Reunion* (2021), and he also lent his voice to the video game *Fallout: New Vegas*.

Perry’s early life was marked by his parents’ separation when he was one year old. He was raised primarily in Ottawa, Canada, by his mother, a journalist, and step-father, a broadcast journalist, though he also spent time in Toronto and Montreal. He attended boarding school at Ashbury College. His childhood included behavioral issues, including theft and fights, which he later attributed to feeling like an outsider. He began drinking at 14 and daily by 18. He was a promising tennis player but abandoned the sport after moving to Los Angeles at 15 to live with his actor father. He then pursued acting, studying at the Buckley School and taking improvisation classes. His early television credits include appearances in *Silver Spoons* and *Growing Pains*.

His breakthrough came with *Friends*, where he was the youngest of the main cast and earned $1 million per episode alongside his co-stars by 2002. While achieving fame, Perry privately battled severe addiction to drugs and alcohol for most of his life. He underwent numerous rehab treatments, including a stay in 2000 for pancreatitis and multiple periods of inpatient care. He struggled with Vicodin, alcohol, and other substances and admitted to having gaps in his memory during filming *Friends* due to his addiction. 

Despite his personal struggles, Perry became a vocal advocate for rehabilitation. He received the Champion of Recovery Award from the White House in 2013 and opened Perry House, a rehab center, though it later relocated. He detailed his experiences in his 2022 memoir, *Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing*, which became a bestseller. 

Perry died on October 28, 2023, at the age of 54, from an accidental drowning caused by the acute effects of ketamine. His death was later determined to be contributed to by the effects of buprenorphine. Following his death, five individuals were charged with aiding in obtaining lethal doses of the drug. A funeral was held at Forest Lawn Memorial Park, attended by his family and *Friends* co-stars, and a foundation was established in his name to support those struggling with addiction.

title: Theophilus Annorbaah
text:
Theophilus Annorbaah is a Ghanaian professional footballer born on September 17, 1989. He currently plays his club football for Medeama SC, a team based in Tarkwa, Ghana, and also represents the Ghana national football team. Annorbaah’s professional career includes playing for Ashanti Gold SC before joining Medeama SC in May 2011. 

A significant achievement in his club career came on July 14, 2013, when Medeama SC secured a 1-0 victory over Asante Kotoko in the final of the Ghanaian FA Cup. This win marked Annorbaah’s first title with the club. 

His involvement with the Ghana national team began in November 2013, when coach Maxwell Konadu selected him for the 2013 WAFU Nations Cup squad. He played a role in the team’s success, culminating in a first-place finish for Ghana after defeating the Senegal national football team with a score of 3-1. 

Annorbaah continued to represent his country and was also selected for the 2014 African Nations Championship. While the team performed well, they ultimately finished as runners-up in that tournament. The article does not detail any specific goals scored by Annorbaah for the national team, only listing a section dedicated to potential international goals.

Throughout his career, Annorbaah has accumulated several honors. At the club level, he is a Ghanaian FA Cup winner with Medeama SC, having achieved this in 2013.  On the international stage, he is a WAFU Nations Cup winner with Ghana, also from 2013, and was part of the team that reached the final of the 2014 African Nations Championship.

title: Fifi Cooper
text:
Fifi Cooper, born Refilwe Boingotlo Moeketsi on October 24, 1991, is a South African recording artist who began her career as an R&B singer before finding success in rap. She grew up in Montshiwa, Mahikeng, as the youngest of three children, developing her singing and dancing abilities from a young age. She completed her secondary education at Batswana High School and later studied Media at Boston Media House.

Cooper’s professional music journey began in 2008 with a guest appearance on Mo'Molemi’s album. Her breakthrough arrived in 2010 with the release of the rap single “Chechela Morago,” which gained significant radio play and established her in the South African music scene. Before achieving solo success, she contributed vocals to remixes of songs by artists like AKA, Mo'Molemi, Khuli Chana and Lection.

In 2015, she signed with Ambitiouz Entertainment and released the AB Crazy-produced song “Kisses,” accompanied by a music video. Later that year, she released her debut studio album, *20FIFI*, which proved highly successful, winning three awards at the 15th Metro FM Music Awards and earning nominations for “Best Newcomer of The Year” and “Best Female Artist of The Year” at the South African Music Awards. 

Cooper’s time with Ambitiouz Entertainment ended in 2017 when she, along with A-Reece and B3nchMarQ, left the label. This departure led to a legal battle, with Ambitiouz successfully suing her for copyright infringement after she resigned without a clearance certificate. The court ruled she forfeited ownership of music recorded under the label and ordered her to remove or return all copies, as well as pay damages and legal fees. However, Julius Malema and the Economic Freedom Fighters intervened, negotiating an out-of-court settlement that restored her rights to her music.

Following the resolution of her legal issues, Fifi Cooper established her own record label, Mo Cooper Records, and released the 21-track album *Take Me Back*, featuring collaborations with artists like Thabsie and Moozlie. In 2020, she released the single “Net So” from her upcoming album, *Chapters*, and followed with “Motlogeleng” in March 2021. 

Known as the “Motswako first lady” by local media, Fifi Cooper is recognized for her versatility, seamlessly blending rap and singing. She is particularly known for her work in hip hop and Motswako, including her contribution as a vocalist on Khuli Chana's hit "Mnatebawen." She describes her rap style as “unpredictable, punchy and hearty.” Fifi Cooper is also a single mother to a son named Resego.

title: Naz Mitrou-Long
text:
Nazareth Jersey Mitrou-Long, born in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada on August 3, 1993, is a professional basketball player currently with AEK Athens of the Greek Basketball League and Basketball Champions League. His father is of Trinidadian descent and his mother is a Greek Canadian, born in Sparta, Greece, and immigrated to Canada as a child. He has a large family, with three siblings and six half-siblings, including brother Elijah, who also played college basketball. Mitrou-Long began his basketball journey playing high school ball at Father Michael Goetz, followed by stints at Montrose Christian, Findlay Prep, and REDA Red before committing to Iowa State University in 2012.

At Iowa State, Mitrou-Long played college basketball for five seasons, experiencing setbacks due to hip injuries. As a freshman, he saw limited action, averaging 1.4 points. He developed into a key player in his sophomore year, becoming a reliable three-point shooter and averaging 7.1 points while shooting 40% from beyond the arc. His junior season saw increased responsibility, averaging 10.1 points and hitting a team-high 77 three-pointers, despite suffering labral tears in both hips that required surgery. He sat out his senior season to rehab, receiving a medical redshirt. Returning for a fifth year as a redshirt senior, he was named to the All-Big 12 Second Team after averaging 12.0 points and showcasing strong offensive performances, including a career-high 37 points in a game against Drake.

After going undrafted in the 2017 NBA draft, Mitrou-Long played in the NBA Summer League for the Sacramento Kings and signed a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz, splitting time between the Jazz and their G League affiliate, the Salt Lake City Stars. He briefly played 20 regular-season games for the Jazz and Indiana Pacers before continuing his career primarily in the G League with the Salt Lake City Stars and Fort Wayne Mad Ants.

Mitrou-Long’s professional career took him to Europe, with stints at Basket Brescia Leonessa in Italy’s Lega Basket Serie A, where he averaged 17.5 points, and Olimpia Milano, the Italian champions. He also played for Žalgiris Kaunas in Lithuania and Olympiacos Piraeus in Greece. He obtained Greek citizenship and a passport in December 2023, allowing him to play as a domestic player for Olympiacos. He has also represented the senior men’s Greek national team, making his debut in November 2024. Throughout his career, Mitrou-Long has been recognized for his three-point shooting ability and work ethic. He began displaying his full last name on his jersey in 2015 to honor his mother.

title: Marcus Aurelius
text:
Marcus Aurelius, born in Rome on April 26th, 121, reigned as Roman Emperor from 161 to 180 AD, and is renowned as a Stoic philosopher. He was the last emperor of the Nerva–Antonine dynasty and the final ruler during the Pax Romana, a period of relative peace lasting nearly two centuries. His lineage connected him, through marriage, to previous emperors Trajan and Hadrian. Orphaned at a young age, Marcus was raised by his mother and grandfather, receiving an education under prominent tutors like Herodes Atticus and Marcus Cornelius Fronto, focusing on both Greek and Latin. 

His path to the throne was carefully orchestrated by Hadrian. After a series of adoptive arrangements, including Hadrian adopting Antoninus Pius, who then adopted Marcus alongside Lucius, the son of a previous heir, Marcus found himself designated as successor. Upon Antoninus Pius’s death in 161, Marcus jointly ruled with Lucius Verus. 

Marcus’s reign was marked by significant military challenges. He faced conflict in the East against a resurgent Parthian Empire and rebellions in Armenia, while simultaneously dealing with incursions from Germanic tribes like the Marcomanni, Quadi, and Sarmatians along the northern borders. These conflicts proved a considerable strain on the empire.  Internally, he oversaw a debasement of the Roman currency, reducing the silver content of the denarius. The Antonine Plague, a devastating epidemic breaking out in 165 or 166, ravaged the empire’s population, potentially claiming five to ten million lives, and may have contributed to Lucius Verus’s death in 169. While persecution of Christians seemingly increased during his rule, there’s little evidence directly implicating Marcus himself, and he even received praise from early Christian writers like Justin Martyr and Tertullian.

Despite the demands of empire, Marcus Aurelius dedicated himself to his philosophical pursuits, writing *Meditations*, a deeply personal work outlining his Stoic beliefs. This work remains a cornerstone of Stoic philosophy and continues to be widely studied today. His reign was followed by that of his son, Commodus, a succession that sparked debate among historians. 

Our understanding of Marcus Aurelius’s life and reign is primarily built upon sources like the *Historia Augusta*, though its reliability is questioned, and the writings of Cassius Dio.  Correspondence with his tutor, Fronto, as well as accounts from physicians like Galen and orators like Aelius Aristides, also provide insights. Physical remnants of his time, like the Column and Equestrian Statue of Marcus Aurelius in Rome, stand as enduring testaments to his legacy. His early life was steeped in aristocratic tradition, marked by a disciplined upbringing focused on intellectual and physical development, and shaped by the expectations placed upon a future leader of Rome.

title: Tony Bellew
text:
Anthony Bellew, born in Liverpool in 1982, was a professional boxer who competed between 2007 and 2018, later transitioning into boxing analysis and commentary. He achieved the WBC cruiserweight title in 2016, adding to his earlier regional successes including the British and Commonwealth light-heavyweight titles held from 2010 to 2014, and the European cruiserweight title from 2015 to 2016. Before turning professional, Bellew was a three-time ABA heavyweight champion as an amateur. Beyond the ring, he is known for portraying boxer Ricky Conlan in the films *Creed* and *Creed III*.

Bellew began his professional career in 2007 with a second-round TKO victory and quickly built a record of early wins. He claimed the vacant Commonwealth light-heavyweight title in 2010, defending it twice, including a hard-fought victory over Ovill McKenzie where both fighters suffered knockdowns. In 2011, a scheduled fight for the WBO light-heavyweight title against Nathan Cleverly fell through due to Bellew missing weight, but he later secured the British light-heavyweight title with another win over McKenzie.

His first encounter with Cleverly in 2011 resulted in a majority decision loss for Bellew. He continued to climb the ranks, defeating Danny McIntosh and Edison Miranda, before securing a WBC Silver title win over Roberto Bolonti in a bruising twelve-round contest. A controversial draw with Isaac Chilemba led to a rematch, which Bellew won by unanimous decision, positioning him as a mandatory challenger for the WBC light-heavyweight title. However, Adonis Stevenson defeated him by TKO in 2013, prompting Bellew to consider moving up to cruiserweight.

Bellew successfully transitioned to cruiserweight, achieving a twelfth-round knockout of Valery Brudov to win the vacant WBO International title in 2014. He then secured a highly anticipated rematch with Nathan Cleverly, this time at cruiserweight, winning by split decision. Following further victories over Ivica Bačurin and Artūrs Kuļikauskis, he challenged for and won the vacant WBC cruiserweight title in 2016, knocking out Ilunga Makabu at Goodison Park. He defended this title with a knockout win over BJ Flores in 2017.

Bellew then moved up to heavyweight for two lucrative fights against David Haye. He defeated Haye in their first encounter in 2017 by TKO after Haye suffered an ankle injury, and again in a rescheduled bout in 2018, winning by TKO in the fifth round after knocking Haye down three times. These fights were significant financial successes, generating substantial pay-per-view revenue and establishing Bellew as a major draw in British boxing.

title: Noel Malicdem
text:
Noel Malicdem, born on January 10, 1977, is a professional darts player from the Philippines who competes in events organized by the Professional Darts Corporation, commonly known as the PDC. He has twice qualified for the PDC World Championship, achieving notable results in both appearances. 

Malicdem first earned a spot in the 2019 World Championship. His debut saw him face Jeffrey de Graaf in the first round, a match he won with a score of 2-3. He then progressed to the second round where he was defeated by Kyle Anderson, losing by a score of 1-3. 

He successfully qualified for the 2020 World Championship through the Asian Tour, finishing in fourth place overall on the tour standings. This qualification marked his second appearance at the prestigious tournament. In his opening match, Malicdem demonstrated strong form, securing a convincing 3-0 victory against Rowby-John Rodriguez. His second-round match against Peter Wright was a particularly close and dramatic contest. Malicdem held a lead and even had opportunities to win the match, possessing match darts, but ultimately was unable to close out the game. The match went to a sudden-death leg, where Peter Wright ultimately prevailed, winning the game 3-2.

Beyond individual championship performances, Malicdem has also represented his country, the Philippines, in team competition. In 2019, he partnered with Lourence Ilagan to compete in the PDC World Cup of Darts. Their participation ended in the first round, as they faced and lost to the team representing England. 

To date, Malicdem’s World Championship record reflects these two appearances. In 2019, he reached the second round before being defeated by Kyle Anderson. He repeated this achievement in 2020, again reaching the second round but losing a closely fought match against Peter Wright. Information regarding his broader PDC performance timeline is available, though the article provides only his World Championship results. Further details about his career statistics and profile can be found on the Darts Database website.

title: Sheldon T. Mills
text:
Sheldon Tibbetts Mills, born in Seattle, Washington on August 13, 1904, and passing away in Santa Barbara, California on July 15, 1988, dedicated his life to a career in the United States Foreign Service. He served as a diplomat with the U.S. Department of State for 32 years, from 1928 until his retirement in 1961. His path to this career began with a Bachelor of Arts degree from Reed College in Portland, Oregon, in 1927, followed by preparation for the rigorous Foreign Service exams under the tutelage of Angus Crawford, a prominent instructor of the time. He successfully passed the exams and was commissioned as a Foreign Service Officer in December 1928. He furthered his education with a detail to Harvard University from 1939 to 1940 to study Economics.

Throughout his career, Mills held postings in a variety of countries, including Bolivia, Panama, Romania, Chile, India, and Brazil. He reached the level of United States Ambassador on three occasions. First, he served as Ambassador to Ecuador from 1954 to 1956. He then moved to Afghanistan, holding the ambassadorship there from 1956 to 1959, where he cultivated a strong rapport with King Mohammad Zahir. This relationship proved valuable to both nations, and the King was later able to return to Afghanistan after years in exile. Notably, during Mills’ time in Afghanistan, the country uniquely received economic development support from both the United States and the Soviet Union, despite the prevailing Cold War tensions. Finally, Mills was appointed as the United States Ambassador to Jordan from 1959 to 1961. 

In Jordan, he established a positive connection with King Hussein, strengthening the relationship between the two countries. A significant moment during his tenure involved a conversation with King Hussein in early 1960, where the King expressed his belief that the long-held Arab aspiration to eliminate Israel should be abandoned, advocating for a pragmatic approach to a final settlement between Israel and the Arab nations.

Mills came from a family with deep roots in American history and prominent figures. His father, Harry Edward Mills, was a Protestant minister and poet, while his mother, Mary Brewster Tibbetts Mills, was a descendant of William Brewster, a passenger on the Mayflower. He married Francesca Dekum in 1932, the daughter of a hardware businessman and a woman whose family also boasted a long American lineage. They had three daughters together. Following his retirement from the Foreign Service, Mills remained engaged in international affairs, becoming an active member of several organizations, including the Channel City Club, the Cosmopolitan Club, the Council on Foreign Relations, the American Foreign Service Association, and Diplomatic and Consular Officials, Retired. He also continued to share his insights through op-ed articles published in local newspapers.

title: Mateo Correa Magallanes
text:
Mateo Correa Magallanes, born July 23, 1866, in Tepechitlán, Zacatecas, Mexico, was a Catholic priest and eventually a saint. He demonstrated early dedication to his faith, attending the seminary in Zacatecas on a scholarship beginning in 1881. He completed his studies and was ordained a priest in 1893 at the age of 27. Early in his priestly service, he administered First Communion to a young Miguel Pro, who would later also become a priest and be martyred himself. 

Correa served as a parish priest in various locations throughout his career. He was first assigned to Concepción del Oro in 1898, and later moved to Colotlán in 1908. The political climate in Mexico during this period was increasingly hostile towards the Catholic Church. Following the government’s repression of the church in 1910, Correa was forced to go into hiding to continue his ministry. He was later assigned to Valparaíso in 1926.

In 1927, during a period of continued persecution, Correa was arrested while performing his priestly duties. Specifically, he was apprehended by soldiers while bringing Viaticum – the Eucharist given to the dying – to a sick woman. He was falsely accused of involvement with the Cristero movement, a Catholic uprising formed in response to the government’s anti-church policies. He was subsequently imprisoned in both Zacatecas and Durango.

While incarcerated in Durango, Correa was approached by General Eulogio Ortiz. Ortiz requested that Correa hear the confessions of imprisoned Cristero rebels. Correa agreed to administer the Sacrament of Reconciliation, fulfilling his priestly obligation. However, following the confessions, Ortiz demanded that Correa reveal what had been said during the sacrament. Correa resolutely refused to violate the seal of confession, despite Ortiz threatening him with immediate execution, even pointing a gun to his head. He maintained his refusal, upholding the sanctity of the confessional. As a result, on February 6, 1927, Correa was taken to a cemetery outside Durango and executed by being shot in the head.

Decades later, on May 21, 2000, Pope John Paul II formally recognized Correa’s martyrdom and canonized him as a saint in a ceremony held in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican. The event drew thousands of pilgrims from Mexico and around the globe. During his homily, Pope John Paul II lauded Correa’s courageous faith and willingness to sacrifice his life for the Gospel, and encouraged all the faithful to emulate his example in their own lives, particularly when facing persecution and violence. Saint Mateo Correa Magallanes is now revered as a symbol of unwavering faith and dedication to Christ.

title: Yordanka Donkova
text:
Yordanka Lyubchova Donkova, born on September 28, 1961, is a retired Bulgarian hurdling athlete who achieved significant success throughout her career, culminating in Olympic and European championship medals, as well as a long-standing world record. She distinguished herself as a dominant force in the 100-meter hurdles, earning a total of sixteen medals from major athletics tournaments. 

Donkova’s career highlights include winning a gold medal and a bronze medal at the Olympic Games. She was particularly celebrated for her performance in 1986, a year in which she broke the 100-meter hurdles world record not once, but four times. She initially equaled the existing record with a time of 12.36 seconds in August, then improved upon it to 12.35 seconds just days later. Further improvements followed, with times of 12.29 and 12.26 seconds also achieved during that same year. 

Her most enduring record was set on August 20, 1988, when she recorded a time of 12.21 seconds. This record stood as the world’s best for almost 28 years, finally being surpassed by Kendra Harrison in 2016.  Throughout her career, Donkova also demonstrated consistent national success, achieving the title of Bulgarian National Champion in the 100-meter hurdles five times – in 1980, 1982, 1984, 1986, and 1994.

Beyond her athletic achievements, Donkova faced a personal challenge early in life, having lost two fingers on her right hand due to a childhood accident. Later in life, she became a mother to three children: a son, Zhivko Atanasov, who became a professional football player currently playing for Cherno More, and twin daughters, Daniela and Desislava, born in 1996. 

Despite receiving an offer to compete for the United States after the 1988 Seoul Olympics, Donkova chose to remain loyal to her home country and continued to represent Bulgaria throughout her career. Recognition of her achievements came in 1986 when she was named Bulgarian Sportsperson of the Year, and also received the title of BTA Best Balkan Athlete of the Year, furthering her legacy as a celebrated athlete both nationally and regionally.

title: Gulshan Kumar
text:
Gulshan Kumar Dua, born in 1956, was a prominent Indian film and music producer who founded the T-Series music label, a cornerstone of the Bollywood industry. His story began with humble roots; his family were Punjabi Hindu refugees who settled in Delhi after the 1947 partition of India, and his father worked as a fruit juice vendor. Gulshan Kumar himself began working with his father from a young age.

Deeply religious, Gulshan Kumar was a devoted worshipper of Shiva and Vaishno Devi. This devotion manifested in a free meal service for devotees visiting the Vaishno Devi Temple, started in 1983 and continuing to this day, now managed by his son. His initial foray into business came with his family’s acquisition of a shop selling records and audio cassettes, which provided the foundation for his future success.

He established Super Cassettes Industries, which rapidly grew into a profitable business, eventually leading him to relocate to Mumbai. His first venture into film production was *Lal Dupatta Malmal Ka* in 1989, but it was *Aashiqui* in 1990, with music by Nadeem-Shravan, that truly launched T-Series to prominence.  He produced several other films including *Bahaar Aane Tak*, *Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin*, and *Jeena Marna Tere Sang*.

T-Series quickly became a leading music label, significantly contributing to a boom in the Indian music industry in the early 1990s.  The company’s revenue grew dramatically, from ₹20 crore in 1985 to ₹500 crore by 1997, the year of Gulshan Kumar’s death. Today, T-Series continues to dominate the Indian music market, controlling over 60% of it, and has a substantial international presence with exports to 24 countries and a distribution network of over 2500 dealers.

Tragically, Gulshan Kumar was assassinated on August 12, 1997, outside a temple in Mumbai, shot 16 times. The murder stemmed from his refusal to pay extortion money demanded by the D-Company, a Mumbai underworld organization. Despite receiving threats, he refused to comply. Abdul Rauf Merchant was ultimately convicted for the murder in 2002 and sentenced to life imprisonment, though initial accusations also pointed towards film composer Nadeem Saifi, who fled the country.  

Following his death, T-Series was taken over by his younger brother, Krishan Kumar, and son, Bhushan Kumar. His daughters, Tulsi Kumar and Khushalii Kumar, have both become playback singers. A biographical film about his life, *Mogul – The Gulshan Kumar Story*, was announced in 2017, illustrating his lasting legacy in the Indian music industry.

title: Alice Torriani
text:
Alice Torriani, born on March 25, 1984, is an Italian actor, author, and screenwriter. She began her career after graduating from the Paolo Grassi Drama School in Milan in 2007, immediately landing the female lead in a production of Chekhov’s *Three Sisters* directed by Massimo Castri, which launched her on a year-long Italian tour. She followed this with another female lead role in Gabriele Lavia’s adaptation of Dostoyevsky’s *Memoirs from the House of The Dead*, leading to her participation in the film *Ten Winters*, which won both the David di Donatello prize for Best Debut and the Silver Ribbon for Best First Work in 2010.

Her early work also included involvement with the European Project "Prospero" and Alvis Hermanis’s *The Young Ladies of Wilko*, a production touring extensively throughout Europe over two years.  As an actor, Torriani has appeared in several films including *E’ nata una star* and *D.A.D.*, and has consistently sought to hone her skills through workshops with prominent directors like Luca Ronconi and Antonio Latella, as well as studies at acting studios in Los Angeles and New York.

Torriani’s television work includes a guest appearance on the popular Italian series *Montalbano*, and a role in the fourth season of *Un Passo dal Ciello*. However, she is perhaps best known for her portrayal of Andreina Mandelli in *Il Paradiso delle Signore* (Ladies' Paradise), a RAI television adaptation of Emile Zola’s *Au Bonheur des Dames* that began in 2015. She has also shared the stage with celebrated Italian comedian Franca Valeri in the play *Il cambio dei cavalli* and performed in Romeo Castellucci’s *The Four Seasons Restaurant*.

Beyond acting, Torriani has established herself as an author. Her debut novel, *L'Altra Sete* (A Different Thirst), was published in 2015 by Fandango Libri and went on to represent Italy at the Festival Européen du Premier Roman in Germany in 2016. She published a second novel, *Una Vita a Posto*, with the same publisher in 2018.  She has also worked as a screenwriter, co-writing the screenplay for the TV series *Cleaning your Shit* with Giampiero Judica in 2015, and starring in the resulting series when it was filmed in 2017.

title: Tarik Elyounoussi
text:
Tarik Elyounoussi, born in Al Hoceima, Morocco in 1988, is a former professional footballer who played as a forward or winger and represented the Norway national team. He moved to Norway with his family at the age of eleven, beginning his football journey with Nylende in Fredrikstad before moving to Trosvik. He quickly rose to prominence, being considered Fredrikstad’s most significant talent in decades and earning the Norwegian Young Player of the Year award in both 2006 and 2007, alongside a Norwegian Football Cup victory.

In 2008, despite interest from Premier League clubs, Elyounoussi initially agreed to a deal with Le Mans but ultimately signed a five-year contract with SC Heerenveen for €3.5 million. He made an immediate impact, scoring on his debut and contributing crucial goals in both the league and the UEFA Cup. He later returned to Norway, first on loan to Lillestrøm SK in 2010, then permanently to Fredrikstad FK in 2011. 

A move to Rosenborg followed in 2012, lasting until 2013 when he was sold to 1899 Hoffenheim in Germany.  He then joined Greek side Olympiacos in 2016 for an estimated €1 million, playing a key role in securing their seventh consecutive Super League title and scoring his first goal for the club against Veria F.C. A loan spell with Qarabağ in Azerbaijan in 2017 proved less successful, with limited playing time. 

Elyounoussi continued his career with AIK in Sweden in 2018, where he won the Allsvenskan league title. He then moved to Japan to join Shonan Bellmare in 2020, remaining with the club until the end of the 2023 season, making 103 appearances and scoring five goals. 

Internationally, Elyounoussi made a memorable start to his Norway career, scoring just four minutes into his debut against Uruguay in 2008 – one of the fastest debut goals in the national team’s history. He later captained the national team in friendlies against South Africa and Zambia in 2013, scoring the winning goal against South Africa. He is cousins with fellow Norwegian international footballer, Mohamed Elyounoussi. Throughout his career, he achieved honours including the Norwegian Football Cup with Fredrikstad, the KNVB Cup with Heerenveen, the Greek Super League with Olympiacos, and the Swedish Allsvenskan with AIK.

title: Neil Googe
text:
Neil Googe is a British comic artist with a career spanning several decades and multiple publishers. He began his work in the late 1990s with contributions to titles like *Shotgun Mary* and *2000 AD*, where he worked on several *Judge Dredd* stories. A significant early project was a graphic novel adaptation of the video game *Silent Hill*, completed in 1999, but it was never published due to disagreements with Konami, despite being finished, advertised, and assigned an ISBN. Googe reportedly lost the only copy of the completed work on a CD.

In 2000, Googe co-founded the independent British comic publisher Com.x, where he created *Bazooka Jules*, though only three issues were released. He then transitioned to the American comic book market, collaborating with Gail Simone on *Welcome to Tranquility* for Wildstorm, after previously working on *Majestic*. Further American projects included *Wildcats: World's End* with Christos Gage and the *World of Warcraft* graphic novel *Dark Riders* with Mike Costa, published by DC Comics following the Wildstorm merger. 

Googe continued to contribute to DC Comics with one-shot issues such as *Rose and Thorn*, a *Detective Comics* Harley Quinn issue, a *Legends of the Dark Knight* Harley Quinn installment, and *The Flash*. He also returned to *2000 AD* to work on *Survival Geeks*. Currently, Googe is developing a creator-owned project called *Welcome to the Hood*, planned as both a pen-and-paper role-playing game and a comic series. He is also revisiting *Bazooka Jules* under the name *Bazooka Jules: Tales from Caliber Bay*, reimagining it as a world setting for role-playing games with accompanying comic short stories, and working on other tabletop and RPG products, including a Pathfinder supplement. He intends to continue working on regular comic projects alongside these new ventures.

His extensive bibliography includes work on titles like *Mercy Heights*, *Pulp Sci-fi: “Coy’s Big Score”*, and *Hondo-City Justice*. Several of his works, including *Majestic* and *Welcome to Tranquility*, have been collected into trade paperbacks.

title: Ramkumar Mukhopadhyay
text:
Ramkumar Mukhopadhyay, born on March 8, 1956, is an Indian Bengali writer known for his contributions to both adult and children’s literature. He was born in Calcutta, the son of Ramangamohan Mukhopadhyay and Kanaklata Mukhopadhyay. His education began with attendance at Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandir, a residential college in Belur, where he completed his graduation. He continued his studies at The University of Calcutta, earning a Masters degree in English, and later achieved a Ph.D from Jadavpur University.

Mukhopadhyay’s professional life has been deeply rooted in the literary world. He began his career as the Regional Secretary for East India with the Sahitya Akademi, and previously served as the Convener of the Bengali Advisory Board for the same organization. He also held the position of President of the Bharatiya Bhasha Parishad. He concluded his career as the Director of the Publishing Department at Visva-Bharati, from which he has since retired. Throughout his career, he has maintained connections with numerous Bengali Little Magazines, indicating a consistent engagement with the smaller, more experimental side of Bengali literary culture.

His published works span a variety of genres. He debuted as an author in 1984 with “Madale Natun Bol” (The New Beats on the Drum), a collection of fourteen short stories. His first novel, “Charane Prantare” (At the Grazing Ground, at the Horizon), followed in 1993. Beyond novels and short stories, Mukhopadhyay has also written travelogues, books of essays, compiled and edited works, and dedicated efforts towards juvenile literature, demonstrating a broad range of literary interests.

Over the course of his career, Mukhopadhyay has received significant recognition for his writing. He was awarded the Somenchandra Award from the Paschimbanga Bangla Akademi in 2000. This was followed by the Galpamela Puraskar in 2004, and the Katha Award in New Delhi in 2005. Further accolades include the Bankimchandra Smriti Puraskar from the Department of Higher Education, Government of West Bengal, in 2006, and the Saratchandra Smriti Puraskar from Bhagalpur in 2007. He received the Sis Puraskar in 2008, the Gajendra Kumar Mitra Birth Centenary Award in 2009, and the prestigious Ananda Puraskar from the Ananda Bazar Patrika and Desh in 2013. More recent awards include the D.L.Ray Award and the Kusumanjali Award, both in 2014, the Krititwa Samagra Puraskar from the Bharatiya Bhasha Parisad in 2016, and the Karmayogi Nanigopal Chakraborty Smriti Sahitya Puraskar in 2023. These awards reflect a sustained and highly regarded presence in Bengali literary circles.

title: Fuerza Guerrera
text:
Fuerza Guerrera, born December 13, 1953, is a veteran Mexican *luchador* (professional wrestler) who debuted in 1977 and continues to wrestle today. He is known for wearing a mask throughout his career, a common practice in Mexican wrestling where a wrestler’s identity is often kept private. His real name is unknown, though it's established his paternal surname is González, the same as his son, Juventud Guerrera.

Guerrera began training in 1977 under Dick Angelo and several other trainers, initially wrestling as “Cachorro González” before adopting the name Fuerza Guerrera – meaning “Warrior Strength” – in 1979. He quickly established himself as a *rudo* (villain) character, a role that suited his personality and wrestling style. He found early success in Empresa Mexicana de Lucha Libre (EMLL, later CMLL), debuting on a major show in 1981 and winning the Mexican National Lightweight Championship in 1983. He later moved up in weight class, capturing the Mexican National Welterweight Championship in 1985 and eventually the NWA World Welterweight Championship in 1988, holding it for a significant period with numerous defenses.

Throughout the 1990s, Fuerza Guerrera became a central figure in the rivalry between CMLL and the newly formed Asistencia Asesoría y Administración (AAA). He followed Antonio Peña, the founder of AAA, when he left CMLL, bringing the intense feud with Octagón with him.  He became the first CMLL World Welterweight Champion in 1992 before moving to AAA. In AAA, he teamed with his son, Juventud Guerrera, achieving success including winning the Mexican National Tag Team Championship. He also held various titles in AAA and the World Wrestling Association (WWA), including WWA Tag Team and Trios Championships. 

A defining aspect of his career involved *Luchas de Apuesta* (bet matches), where wrestlers risk their masks. Fuerza Guerrera participated in several high-stakes matches, most notably a three-way round robin with Octagón and Huracán Ramírez in 1990, ultimately forcing Ramírez to unmask. He also famously avoided losing his own mask in a tag team match against El Hijo del Santo and Black Shadow Jr. 

In later years, Guerrera returned to CMLL briefly in 2001, winning the CMLL World Trios Championship. He eventually settled with the International Wrestling Revolution Group (IWRG) in 2007, where he continues to wrestle. He has held the IWRG Intercontinental Welterweight Championship multiple times.  He's also helped his son establish a new promotion, Gran Prix Championship Wrestling Super-X.  Despite a strained relationship with his son, and a one-time match against him in 2007, both have expressed a desire for a *Luchas de Apuesta* match before retirement. Fuerza Guerrera has also expanded his family's presence in wrestling, presenting his other children as professional wrestlers in 2018.

title: Phillip Gillespie
text:
Phillip J. Gillespie, born on October 23, 1975, in Frankston, Victoria, Australia, is an Australian cricket umpire who previously played the sport. He currently serves as a member of the Australian National Umpire Panel. Gillespie’s path to umpiring began after a series of injuries – to his Achilles tendon, jaw, and knee – sustained while playing for the Rowville Cricket Club in Melbourne forced him to find another way to remain involved in cricket. He started his umpiring career in the Victorian Premier Cricket competition in 2009.

His first List A match was in February 2013, officiating a game between the England Lions and Victoria, and he went on to umpire eight matches in the Matador BBQs One-Day Cup. He also officiated in women’s cricket, including two Women’s National Cricket League matches, notably the semi-final between New South Wales and Victoria in 2015. Gillespie was involved in the Big Bash League, umpiring six matches in the 2015–16 season and four more the following season. He began umpiring women’s Twenty20 matches during the 2012–13 Australian Women's Twenty20 Cup, and stood in a Women’s Big Bash League semi-final in the 2016–17 season, a match between the Sydney Sixers and the Hobart Hurricanes.

Gillespie’s first-class debut occurred on February 15, 2015, in a Sheffield Shield match between New South Wales and Victoria, a game remembered for Doug Bollinger’s hat-trick from Gillespie’s end of the pitch. He subsequently umpired nine further first-class matches, with his most recent being a clash between Tasmania and Queensland in March 2017. 

He made his international umpiring debut in 2014 during the West Indies women’s tour of Australia, officiating all four Women's One Day International matches. He continued to umpire in international women’s cricket, including the final two WODIs of the South Africa in Australia series in November 2016.  He also officiated matches in the 2016–17 ICC World Cricket League East Asia–Pacific Region Qualifiers in February 2017, covering fixtures involving Fiji, the Philippines, and Vanuatu.

Gillespie’s dedication to improving his skills led to his acceptance into the 2015 intake of the Australian Sports Commission National Officiating Scholarship program, designed to support the development of elite-level officials. In May 2015, he joined the 2015–16 National Umpire Panel, replacing Damien Mealey.  He further progressed his career, standing in his first Twenty20 International (T20I) match between Australia and West Indies on October 7, 2022. 

Outside of cricket, Gillespie works as a police officer in the Victorian Police Force and is a supporter of the Richmond Tigers Australian Football League team.

title: Julie Bishop
text:
Julie Bishop was born in Lobethal, South Australia in 1956, the third of four children. Her parents were both involved in local politics, and she grew up on an apple and cherry orchard. She was educated at Basket Range Primary School and St Peter's Collegiate Girls’ School, where she was head prefect, before studying law at the University of Adelaide, graduating in 1978. After a brief stint at an Adelaide law firm, she moved to Perth in 1983 after marrying property developer Neil Gillon, and became a partner at Robinson Cox, later Clayton Utz, eventually becoming managing partner of the Perth office. Prior to entering politics, she held positions with the Special Broadcasting Service and the senate of Murdoch University.

Bishop entered federal parliament in 1998, representing the Division of Curtin in Western Australia. In the Howard government, she held portfolios including Minister for Ageing, Education and Science, and Women. Following the Coalition’s loss in the 2007 election, she was elected as the first female Deputy Leader of the Liberal Party, a position she held for eleven years under three different leaders: Brendan Nelson, Malcolm Turnbull, and Tony Abbott. 

When the Coalition regained power in 2013, Bishop became Australia’s first female Minister for Foreign Affairs. During her tenure, she oversaw changes to the foreign aid program, including integrating AusAID into the Department of Foreign Affairs and implementing significant budget cuts. She also navigated complex international issues such as the military intervention against ISIL, the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, and the execution of Australian citizens in Indonesia. She also initiated the New Colombo Plan, providing funding for Australian students to study in the Indo-Pacific region.

In 2018, a leadership spill within the Liberal Party saw Scott Morrison elected as party leader and Prime Minister, defeating both Peter Dutton and Bishop. Bishop declined to remain as Foreign Minister and moved to the backbench, subsequently announcing her retirement from politics in February 2019, taking effect after the federal election was called. 

Since leaving parliament, Bishop has continued to serve in public life. In January 2020, she became the first female chancellor of the Australian National University. In April 2024, she was appointed as a United Nations special envoy for Myanmar. Before entering politics, Bishop was involved in a significant legal case defending CSR Limited against compensation claims from asbestos mining workers, an involvement that later drew scrutiny after she became a public figure, though she maintained she acted ethically and professionally. Her early political involvement included serving as a delegate to the 1998 constitutional convention, where she advocated for a minimalist approach to republicanism.

title: Kiara Advani
text:
Kiara Advani, born Alia Advani on July 31, 1991, is a leading Indian actress working in both Hindi and Telugu cinema. She is among the highest-paid actresses in India and has received an IIFA Award and two Zee Cine Awards, with nominations for two Filmfare Awards recognizing her work. Her acting journey began with the 2014 film *Fugly*, which didn’t perform well, but she persevered. A significant turning point came with *M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story* (2016), where she portrayed cricketer MS Dhoni’s wife, Sakshi Rawat, achieving commercial success. She further showcased her range with a role in the Netflix anthology *Lust Stories* (2018), playing a sexually dissatisfied wife, earning critical praise.

While her Telugu debut, *Bharat Ane Nenu* (2018), was a commercial success, her subsequent Telugu film *Vinaya Vidheya Rama* was not. 2019 proved to be a breakthrough year with *Kabir Singh* and *Good Newwz*, both becoming major box office hits. She won an IIFA Award for Best Supporting Actress for her performance in *Good Newwz*.  She continued to gain prominence with commercially successful films like *Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2* and *Jugjugg Jeeyo* in 2022.

Advani has received critical acclaim for roles in *Shershaah* (2021), where she played Vikram Batra’s girlfriend, and *Satyaprem Ki Katha* (2023), portraying a troubled married woman, both earning her Filmfare Award nominations for Best Actress.  She has also appeared in films like *Guilty*, *Laxmii*, *Indoo Ki Jawani*, *Govinda Naam Mera*, and most recently, *Game Changer* (2025) though the latter didn't perform as expected. She is currently involved in several upcoming projects including *War 2* and *Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups*.

Beyond acting, Advani is a sought-after brand ambassador, endorsing products like Audi, Galaxy Chocolate, and Colgate, among others. She made her debut at the Met Gala in 2025, notably appearing with a baby bump. She is married to actor Sidharth Malhotra since February 2023, and they have a daughter born in July 2025.

Advani’s background reveals a family with connections to the Indian film industry; actors Ashok Kumar and Saeed Jaffrey are relatives through her maternal side. She holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in mass communication from Jai Hind College, Mumbai. Originally named Alia Advani, she adopted the name Kiara at the suggestion of Salman Khan to avoid confusion with the already established actress Alia Bhatt.  She is regarded as charming and energetic, and has been recognized on lists like The Times of India’s “Most Desirable Woman” and GQ India’s “30 Most Influential Young Indians”. In 2023, she was the most searched personality on Google in India and is among India’s highest tax-paying celebrities.

title: Caitlin Lowe
text:
Caitlin Faith Lowe-Nagy, born February 6, 1985, is currently the head coach of the Arizona Wildcats softball team. Her career began with significant success at Foothill High School in California, where she was a four-time All-American and led her team to multiple championships between 2000 and 2003, earning Orange County “Player of the Year” in 2003. She continued her athletic accomplishments at the University of Arizona, playing softball and achieving First Team All-American status in each of her four years – a feat only shared by one other Wildcat player. 

During her time at Arizona, Lowe led the team to back-to-back Women’s College World Series championships in 2006 and 2007. She consistently ranked among the program’s leaders in stolen bases, runs, and batting average, and her career included impressive single-game performances, such as a four-hit game against Louisiana Tech and driving in four RBIs against Louisiana-Lafayette. She accumulated over 300 hits, 200 runs, and 100 stolen bases while maintaining a .400 batting average, and was named to the Greatest College Softball Team All-Time in the outfield.  She also earned the inaugural Lowe's Senior CLASS Softball Award, recognizing her excellence both on and off the field.

Following her collegiate career, Lowe competed internationally, winning a silver medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics. She was a member of the U.S. Women’s National Softball Team from 2005, contributing to World Cup wins in 2006 and 2007, and a gold medal at the 2007 Pan American Games. She was known for her exceptional speed and base running, even hitting the first-ever inside-the-park home run in Olympic Games history. 

Lowe then spent six seasons playing professionally with the USSSA Pride in National Pro Fastpitch, winning three titles and being named Player of the Year in 2012. She retired from professional play in 2015, after which the Pride inducted her into their Hall of Fame and retired her jersey number 26.

After her playing career, Lowe transitioned into coaching. She began as a volunteer assistant coach at Arizona in 2013, becoming the associate head coach by 2018. In June 2021, she was named the head coach of the Wildcats, following the retirement of long-time coach Mike Candrea. 

Lowe graduated from Arizona with a degree in psychology and a minor in communications. She comes from an athletic family, with her sister and another sister also playing softball at Oregon State University. She is married to Paul Nagy, an assistant soccer coach at the University of Arizona, and they have two children, Harper and Beckham.

title: David Bogue
text:
David Bogue was a Scottish religious leader born on February 18, 1750, at Hallydown Farm in Berwickshire, Scotland. He was the son of farmer John Bogue and Margaret Swanston, and initially received his education in Eyemouth. Following his studies in Divinity at Edinburgh University, he was authorized to preach by the Church of Scotland. However, unable to secure a position within Scotland, he moved to London in 1771. There he worked as a teacher in schools located in Edmonton, Hampstead, and Camberwell.

In 1777, Bogue became the minister of an independent Congregational church in Gosport, Hampshire, succeeding James Watson and Thomas Williams in that role. He is particularly remembered for establishing an institution in 1771 dedicated to training men for the ministry. This academy played a crucial role in the formation of the London Missionary Society, effectively serving as its initial foundation. By 1800, the London Missionary Society was formally sending prospective missionaries to Bogue for preparation.
