The novel delves into the complexities of American immigration, the pursuit of the American Dream, and the financial and emotional struggles experienced by immigrants. Mbue herself has stated that the characters’ experiences mirror her own, encompassing financial hardship, feelings of hopelessness, and a reassessment of personal goals. She believes strongly in the power of literature to foster empathy, particularly in areas like immigration and politics where she feels it is lacking. Her second novel, *How Beautiful We Were*, published in 2021, shifts focus to the environmental crisis unfolding in Africa, attributing it to corporate greed.

Mbue became a U.S. citizen in 2014 and now lives in New York City with her husband and children. *Behold the Dreamers* was acquired by Random House in a million-dollar deal and was praised for its nuanced portrayal of the United States. Its release coincided with the 2016 presidential election and its accompanying anti-immigrant rhetoric, bringing attention to the obstacles faced by those seeking to achieve the American Dream. The novel’s impact was further amplified when it was selected for Oprah Winfrey’s book club in 2017. She also contributed to the anthology *New Daughters of Africa* in 2019. 

Her works have been translated into multiple languages, including French and German. Her published novels are *Behold the Dreamers* (2016), *How Beautiful We Were* (2021), and their respective translations.

title: Napoleon
text:
Napoleon Bonaparte, born Napoleone di Buonaparte in Corsica in 1769, rose from relative obscurity to become one of the most significant figures in European history. His family, of Italian noble descent, moved to mainland France when he was young, and he was commissioned as an officer in the French Royal Army in 1785. He initially supported the French Revolution, even promoting its ideals in Corsica, and rapidly ascended through the ranks, gaining recognition for his successful siege of Toulon in 1793 and for suppressing a royalist uprising in Paris in 1795.

His military prowess truly emerged during the War of the First Coalition in 1796, where he led a campaign in Italy against Austria and its allies, achieving decisive victories that cemented his status as a national hero. This success was followed by an expedition to Egypt and Syria in 1798, undertaken as a means to disrupt British trade routes and further his political ambitions. In 1799, he seized power in France through the Coup of 18 Brumaire, becoming First Consul of the Republic. He consolidated his control with the victory at the Battle of Marengo in 1800, securing France’s position in the War of the Second Coalition, and later sold the Louisiana Territory to the United States in 1803. 

Napoleon’s ambition culminated in his self-coronation as Emperor of the French in 1804. He then embarked on a series of conflicts, known as the Napoleonic Wars, dominating much of continental Europe. Major victories at Austerlitz in 1805 resulted in the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire, and at Jena-Auerstedt in 1806, he defeated Prussia. He installed his brother Joseph as King of Spain in 1808, sparking the Peninsular War. Further victories followed at Wagram in 1809, but his disastrous invasion of Russia in 1812, marked by a devastating retreat from Moscow, proved to be a turning point. 

Following defeats at the Battle of Leipzig in 1813, Napoleon was forced to abdicate in 1814 and was exiled to the island of Elba.  In a remarkable return, he escaped Elba in 1815 and briefly regained control of France, initiating the period known as the Hundred Days. This final chapter ended with his definitive defeat at the Battle of Waterloo in June 1815. He was then exiled to the remote island of Saint Helena, where he died of stomach cancer in 1821 at the age of 51.

Napoleon’s legacy is complex. He is revered as a military genius, and his tactics continue to be studied. He instituted significant legal and administrative reforms, including the Napoleonic Code, which modernized laws and centralized state power. He abolished feudalism, emancipated religious minorities, and established a public education system. However, he is also criticized for the immense loss of life caused by his wars, his looting of conquered lands, his suppression of free speech, and the reinstatement of slavery in French colonies (with the exception of Haiti). His reign saw a curtailment of representative government and the violent repression of opposition.

title: Daniel Ek
text:
Daniel Ek, born in Stockholm, Sweden in 1983, is a businessman and technologist best known as the co-founder and CEO of the music streaming service Spotify. As of May 2025, Forbes estimates his net worth to be $9.2 billion. He grew up in the Rågsved district and briefly attended the KTH Royal Institute of Technology before dropping out to pursue a career in IT.

Ek’s early career involved building websites and working with open-source technologies from a young age. He held positions at companies like Jajja, Tradera (later acquired by eBay), and Stardoll, serving as CTO for the latter. He also founded Advertigo, an online advertising company, which he sold to TradeDoubler in 2006. Following this, he briefly led μTorrent before its sale to BitTorrent, and Ludvig Strigeus, a developer from μTorrent, later joined him at Spotify.

The idea for Spotify arose in 2002, observing the difficulties in combating music piracy after the shutdown of Napster. Ek envisioned a legal streaming service that would offer a superior alternative to piracy while providing compensation to the music industry. He co-founded Spotify AB with Martin Lorentzon in 2006, launching the service in 2008. Originally utilizing a peer-to-peer model, Spotify transitioned to a server-client system in 2014. Lorentzon stepped down as chairman in 2016, with Ek assuming the role alongside his duties as CEO. By 2017, Spotify had over 217 million active users and had garnered over $2.5 billion in funding. Ek was named the most powerful person in the music industry by Billboard that same year, and in 2022, he personally invested $50 million in Spotify stock.

Beyond Spotify, Ek co-founded Neko Health in 2018, a medical technology company focused on non-invasive full-body scanning using AI, which launched in 2023. He also established Prima Materia in 2021, an investment firm with a $1 billion pledge to support European technology “moonshots,” and serves as chairman of German defense technology company Helsing, a recipient of significant investment from Prima Materia.

Ek has been vocal about the challenges facing startups in Sweden, co-authoring an open letter in 2016 advocating for changes to laws concerning housing, taxation, and education to prevent companies like Spotify from relocating. He has also offered insights into the evolving music industry, suggesting artists need to focus on continuous engagement with fans rather than infrequent album releases. Recent comments regarding the “shelf life” of content sparked criticism from musicians, leading to clarifications from Ek emphasizing his support for creative expression. 

Personally, Ek is married to Sofia Levander and has two daughters. He's a supporter of Arsenal Football Club and made an unsuccessful bid to purchase the team in 2021. His story was depicted in the 2022 Netflix series *The Playlist*, where he was portrayed by Edvin Endre. His views and Spotify’s business practices have faced criticism from artists concerned about fair compensation and the impact on the music industry, prompting Spotify to release annual artist remuneration reports. Some artists have even removed their music from Spotify in protest of Prima Materia’s investments in defense technology.

title: Richie Dorman
text:
Richie Dorman, born on June 14, 1988, is a Welshman who has transitioned from a professional football player to a sporting director role. He currently holds the position of sporting director for Burton Albion, a League One club. Dorman originates from Hawarden in Wales, and is the brother of another footballer, Andy Dorman.

His footballing career began with time in the academy system of English club Blackburn Rovers. In 2006, Dorman moved to the United States where he played for the New Hampshire Phantoms. While residing in the US, he also participated in amateur football with the Boston University Terriers. He eventually returned to Wales for two separate periods with Airbus UK. 

Dorman then ventured into Finnish football, initially joining Kraft on loan in April 2011. He later became a more established player with SJK, a club where he would achieve significant success. His performances for SJK were recognized in June 2014 when he was selected for the Veikkausliiga 'Team of the Month'. 

After his playing career concluded, Dorman remained with SJK, but in a different capacity. On October 30, 2018, he was appointed as the club’s technical director. He held this position for several years before moving back to Britain. 

In May 2023, Dorman departed SJK and took on the role of sporting director at Burton Albion. During his time with SJK as a player, the club enjoyed a period of success, winning several trophies. These included the Veikkausliiga title in 2015, the Finnish Cup in 2016, and the Finnish League Cup in 2014. Prior to their Veikkausliiga win, SJK also secured the Ykkönen title in 2012, demonstrating a climb through the Finnish football league system.

title: Erich Hartmann
text:
Erich Alfred Hartmann, born in 1922, was the most successful fighter ace in the history of aerial warfare, amassing 352 aerial victories during World War II while flying for the Luftwaffe. He completed 1,404 combat missions and engaged in 825 aerial combats, shooting down 345 Soviet and 7 American aircraft. Remarkably, Hartmann was never shot down himself, though he was forced to crash-land his fighter 16 times due to mechanical failures or damage from enemy fire.

Hartmann’s journey began with gliding, a passion fostered by his parents, both of whom were involved in aviation. He joined the Luftwaffe in 1940 and completed his fighter pilot training in 1942, subsequently being assigned to the highly experienced Jagdgeschwader 52 (JG 52) on the Eastern Front. There, he learned from veteran pilots, developing his tactical skills. He steadily increased his kill count, earning the Knight’s Cross of the Iron Cross in October 1943 for 148 victories, then the Oak Leaves to the Knight’s Cross in March 1944 for 202 victories. In August 1944, he received the Swords to the Knight's Cross with Oak Leaves, culminating in the Knight’s Cross with Oak Leaves, Swords and Diamonds for 301 victories – Germany’s highest military decoration at the time.

Hartmann’s early combat experience was marked by a lack of discipline, resulting in a temporary grounding after recklessly pursuing an engagement and crashing due to fuel exhaustion. He learned from his mistakes and adopted a tactical approach emphasizing observation, decisive action, and close-range attacks, influenced by experienced pilots like Paule Roßmann. He became known as "Bubi" (kid) by his colleagues. He proved particularly successful during the intense fighting around Kursk in July 1943, becoming an “ace-in-a-day” multiple times, claiming as many as seven victories in a single day. By August 1943, he had accumulated 90 victories and was appointed Staffelkapitän (squadron leader).

Hartmann’s success stemmed from a combination of skill and a pragmatic assessment of Soviet pilot capabilities and equipment. He initially believed Soviet pilots were poorly trained and equipped, with rudimentary gunsights, and he learned valuable techniques from captured airmen to address problems like cold-weather engine starting. He emphasized careful assessment of the combat situation over aggressive maneuvering. 

His final victory came on May 8, 1945, just hours before Germany’s surrender. He and his unit surrendered to US forces, but were handed over to the Soviets. Accused of war crimes in an attempt to coerce him into joining the Soviet-aligned East German air force, he was sentenced to 25 years of imprisonment and spent ten years in Soviet prison camps and gulags before being released in 1955. He was posthumously exonerated by Russia in 1997.

After his release, Hartmann joined the newly formed West German Air Force in 1956 and became the first Geschwaderkommodore (wing commander) of Jagdgeschwader 71 “Richthofen”. He retired in 1970 due to disagreements over the procurement of the F-104 Starfighter, over safety concerns, and later worked as a civilian flight instructor. He died in 1993 at the age of 71. His early life was impacted by his family’s move from Germany to China and back, and his brother also served in the Luftwaffe during the war.

title: Karl Urban
text:
Karl Urban is a New Zealand actor born on June 7, 1972, who began his career with roles in New Zealand film and television, including a small part in the series *Pioneer Woman*. He gained wider recognition with his first Hollywood role in the 2002 horror film *Ghost Ship*. Since then, he has appeared in numerous high-profile films, notably playing Éomer in *The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers* and *The Return of the King*, Vaako in two *Riddick* films, and Dr. Leonard “Bones” McCoy in the *Star Trek* reboot series – a role he actively pursued as a longtime fan of the franchise. Other significant film roles include parts in *The Bourne Supremacy*, *Doom*, *Dredd*, *Pete's Dragon*, and *Thor: Ragnarok*.

Urban’s early life was influenced by his father, a German immigrant who ran a leather goods store, and his mother, who worked in the film industry, exposing him to New Zealand cinema. He showed an early aptitude for performance at St Mark's Church School and briefly studied at Victoria University of Wellington before dedicating himself to acting. Before landing Hollywood roles, he worked in local TV commercials and theatre, and even spent time in Australia.

Beyond his film work, Urban has also had success in television. He starred in the sci-fi series *Almost Human* in 2013 and, since 2019, has gained significant acclaim for his portrayal of Billy Butcher in the Amazon Prime Video series *The Boys*. He also played Detective John Kennex in the series *Almost Human*, a futuristic police drama.

Urban’s dedication to his craft is demonstrated by his thorough preparation for roles, like his meticulous approach to embodying Dr. McCoy from *Star Trek*. While considered for the role of James Bond, he ultimately did not take on the part. He has also lent his voice to animated projects, including *The Sea Beast* in 2022, and even had a cameo appearance as a stormtrooper in *Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker*.

In his personal life, Urban was married to Natalie Wihongi, his former makeup artist, from 2004 until their separation in 2014; they have two sons, Hunter and Indiana. He was later in a relationship with actress Katee Sackhoff from 2014 to 2018. He is also involved in philanthropic work, serving as a celebrity ambassador for KidsCan, a New Zealand charity supporting disadvantaged children, and as an official Ambassador for UNICEF Aotearoa New Zealand. He participated in a *Reunited Apart* special alongside other *Lord of the Rings* cast members to raise money for charity.

title: Alfred Hitchcock
text:
Alfred Hitchcock was a highly influential English film director, born in 1899 and passing away in 1980, who directed over 50 feature films across six decades. He became widely known as the "Master of Suspense," achieving celebrity status through his films, frequent cameo appearances within them, interviews, and his work hosting and producing the television series *Alfred Hitchcock Presents*. Despite receiving 46 Academy Award nominations and winning six, he was never awarded Best Director, though he was nominated five times.

Hitchcock began his film career in 1919 as a title card designer after working as a technical clerk and copywriter. His directorial debut came with the 1925 British-German silent film *The Pleasure Garden*. He gained significant recognition with *The Lodger: A Story of the London Fog* (1927), a film that helped define the thriller genre, and *Blackmail* (1929), which was Britain’s first “talkie.” His films *The 39 Steps* (1935) and *The Lady Vanishes* (1938) are considered among the best British films of the 20th century. In 1939, producer David O. Selznick brought him to Hollywood, where he directed a series of successful films including *Rebecca* (1940), which won the Academy Award for Best Picture, *Foreign Correspondent* (1940), *Suspicion* (1941), *Shadow of a Doubt* (1943), *Notorious* (1946), *Lifeboat* (1944), *Spellbound* (1945), *Rear Window* (1954), and *Psycho* (1960), the latter earning him another Oscar nomination. 

Throughout his career, Hitchcock frequently collaborated with prominent actors, directing Cary Grant in four films, James Stewart in four, Ingrid Bergman in three, and a consecutive run of three with Grace Kelly. He became an American citizen in 1955. His filmography includes other notable works such as *Rope* (1948), *Strangers on a Train* (1951), *Dial M for Murder* (1954), *To Catch a Thief* (1955), *The Birds* (1963), *Marnie* (1964) and *Frenzy* (1972). In 2012, his film *Vertigo* was named the greatest film ever made by the British Film Institute, displacing *Citizen Kane*. As of 2021, nine of his films are preserved in the United States National Film Registry, including his personal favorite, *Shadow of a Doubt*.

Hitchcock’s early life was marked by a disciplined upbringing, the son of a greengrocer. He attended a series of schools, including Jesuit colleges where he developed a sense of fear and was often punished with a “ferula”. He initially studied engineering, but after his father’s death he took a job at the Henley Telegraph and Cable Company, where he began to explore his interest in art and advertising. He entered the film industry through Famous Players–Lasky, beginning as a title card designer and quickly taking on various roles including art direction and scriptwriting. He worked with Gainsborough Pictures and spent time filming in Germany, learning from filmmakers like F. W. Murnau.  He actively promoted himself as a director, believing the director’s name should be synonymous with quality, and gained recognition with early successes like *The Ring* before establishing himself as a master of suspense with *The Lodger*.

title: Ezechiel N'Douassel
text:
Ezechiel Aliadjim N’Douassel, born in 1988, is a Chadian professional footballer currently playing as a striker for Bekasi City. He began his career in 2006 with Tourbillon before moving to Algeria, joining MC Oran and then USM Blida in 2007. It was at USM Blida where he first gained recognition, scoring a brace on his debut and finishing the season with five goals in fifteen appearances. During his time there, he attracted interest from several European clubs, including Olympique de Marseille and Arsenal, but a move to Belgian club FCV Dender in 2009 ultimately fell through due to contractual issues, forcing his return to USM Blida.

In 2011, N’Douassel signed a four-year contract with Tunisian side Club Africain, where he participated in the CAF Confederation Cup, reaching the final in 2011 and the fourth round in 2012, even scoring a hat-trick in the latter competition. A proposed loan move to Paris FC in 2014 was cancelled due to financial difficulties, leaving him seeking a new club.

He then moved to Israel in 2016, initially signing a three-year contract with Ironi Kiryat Shmona, but departed for Hapoel Tel Aviv after only a few months. His time at Hapoel was short-lived, ending in March 2017 due to behavioral concerns. Later that year, he joined Persib Bandung in Indonesia, initially on a half-year deal which was then extended. He quickly became a key player, scoring his first league goal for the club in August 2017 and becoming their top scorer in the 2018 season with 17 goals, including a four-goal performance against PSM Makassar in 2019.

In January 2020, N’Douassel transferred to Bhayangkara, where he made his debut in a pre-season cup, helping the team win the tournament after scoring in a match against Petaling Jaya City. He continued to contribute in the league, scoring his first goal against Persija Jakarta. He further showcased his scoring ability in the 2021 Liga 1 season, achieving braces against Persiraja Banda Aceh and Barito Putera.

Throughout his career, N’Douassel has been a consistent presence in the Chad national team, debuting in 2005. He is the national team's most capped player and all-time leading goalscorer, and has participated in numerous Africa Cup of Nations and World Cup qualifying campaigns, as well as CEMAC Cup tournaments. He was also recognized with the Liga 2 Player of the Half Season and Player of the Month awards for November 2024-25.

title: Maja Jager
text:
Maja Buskbjerg Jager, born December 22, 1991, is a Danish recurve archer who has competed in the Olympic Games in both 2012 and 2020 (held in 2021). She achieved a major career highlight by winning the individual championship at the 2013 World Archery Championships, a feat that earned her the Danish Sports Name of the Year award that same year. Throughout her career, she has also accumulated multiple medals at the European Games and European Archery Championships.

Jager began archery at the age of eight, initially practicing in a warehouse in Tilst, facilitated by her father’s connections as a fruit grower. She later received training from Ole Gammelgaard, a former Danish Olympic archer. A pivotal moment in her career came in 2013 when she moved to Goesan, South Korea, to train under Kim Hyung-Tak, a renowned Olympic coach. This move was part of an agreement between Kim and the Danish Archery Federation, and to fulfill residency requirements, Jager pursued and completed an undergraduate degree in computer system engineering at Jungwon University. She spent five years in South Korea, finding the initial adjustment period to be the most challenging of her life, before returning to Denmark in 2018 and beginning a postgraduate program at the Technical University of Denmark in 2019.

Jager first represented Denmark on the national team at the 2009 Archery World Cup. She participated in the 2010 and 2011 European Archery Championships, achieving ninth place individually in the latter. Her Olympic debut occurred at the 2012 London Summer Olympics, where she competed in the women’s team event alongside Carina Christiansen and Louise Laursen, setting a new Danish national record in the ranking round. 

Her breakthrough came at the 2013 World Championships in Belek, Turkey. Despite a previous lack of success in international competitions, she qualified for the elimination rounds as the eighth seed and proceeded to upset top-ranked archers Ki Bo-bae and Yun Ok-hee. In a dramatic final against Xu Jing, she won by a single millimeter in a one-arrow shoot-off, claiming the world championship title. She also secured a bronze medal in the women’s team event at the same championships. This victory was credited with increasing the popularity of archery in Denmark. 

In subsequent years, Jager continued to compete, winning a silver medal in the mixed team recurve event at the 2014 European Archery Championships and another silver in the women’s individual event at the 2015 European Games. While she didn't defend her world title in 2015, she qualified for and competed in the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021), being eliminated in the second round. She also won a bronze medal in the women’s team competition at the 2019 European Games, and was runner-up in the individual event at the 2018 European Archery Championships.

title: Muhammad Alhamid
text:
Muhammad Alhamid, born in Makassar on September 17, 1971, is an Indonesian professor, academic, civil servant, and figure in electoral oversight. He comes from an Arab Indonesian family of the Ba’Alawi sada clan, the son of Sayyid Alhamid and Syarifah Aisyah Sadiq Alaydrus, and is married to Lubena Umar Alhaddad with whom he has five children: Fatimah Zahra, Jakfar Sodiq, Khadijah, Aisyah, and Umar Muchdar.

His educational background began in Makassar, completing elementary school in 1984, junior high in 1987, and high school in 1990. He then attended Hasanuddin University, earning a Sarjana Ilmu Pemerintahan (Bachelor of Science in Government) in 1994 and a Master of Science degree in 1999 from the same institution. He later pursued and completed his doctoral studies at Airlangga University in 2007, focusing his dissertation on leadership and innovation adoption within a South Sulawesi farming community. 

Alhamid’s academic career includes positions at Hasanuddin University, where he served as secretary of the Political Science Department from 2008 to 2010, and then as its chairman from 2010 to 2012. In 2015, he was confirmed as a professor in Sociology. He has also lectured at the University of West Sulawesi since 2008 and the Makassar Institute of Public Administration since 2010, teaching courses in Indonesian Political Systems, Political Geography, and National Unity and Political Development. He is a prolific publisher, with numerous journal articles covering topics from election accountability and Islamic perspectives on gender to the roles of Nahdlatul Ulama and Muhammadiyah in Indonesian political culture. He also authored a book in 2018 titled *Eksistensi DKPP RI dalam Mengawal Demokrasi dan Pemilu Bermartabat* (The Existence of the DKPP RI in Escorting Dignified Democracy and Elections).

His involvement in election oversight began in 2009 as chairman of the South Sulawesi Province Election Supervisory Committee. He was then appointed a commissioner of the Election Supervisory Board of the Republic of Indonesia (Bawaslu RI) in 2012, subsequently serving as its chairman from 2012 to 2017. Following his tenure at Bawaslu, he was appointed as a member of the Election Organization Ethics Council of the Republic of Indonesia (DKPP RI) in 2017 by President Joko Widodo, a position he held until 2022. 

Alhamid has received recognition for his service, including the Satyalancana Karya Satya award for 10 years of civil service in 2012 and the 1st Class of Star of the Defenders of Democracy award in 2015, presented by President Joko Widodo. This latter award acknowledged his contributions as Chairman of Bawaslu during the 70th anniversary of Indonesian independence.

title: Coco Chanel
text:
Gabrielle Bonheur “Coco” Chanel, born in 1883, was a French fashion designer and businesswoman who revolutionized feminine style in the post-World War I era. She is the only fashion designer to be named on *Time* magazine’s list of the 100 most influential people of the 20th century, and her influence extended beyond clothing to include jewelry, handbags, and fragrance, most famously Chanel No. 5 and the iconic interlocking-CC monogram. Chanel’s couture house closed in 1939 with the outbreak of World War II, but she remained in France during the German occupation, a period marked by controversial collaboration with the occupiers and the Vichy regime. Documents later revealed her direct involvement with Nazi intelligence, including a plan to act as a mediator between the Allies and Germany. She was questioned after the war due to her relationship with German diplomat Hans Günther von Dincklage, but was not charged, reportedly due to the intervention of Winston Churchill.  She eventually returned to Paris in 1954 to revive her fashion house.

Chanel’s early life was marked by hardship. Born to a laundrywoman and an itinerant vendor, she spent her early years in poverty, and her birth was initially registered incorrectly as “Chasnel.”  After her mother's death when she was eleven, she and her siblings were sent to the Aubazine convent, where she learned to sew.  She later worked as a seamstress and cabaret singer, acquiring the nickname “Coco” during her performances, though accounts of its origin vary. She began designing hats as a hobby while living with Étienne Balsan, a wealthy French officer, who provided her with financial support and access to a privileged social circle. 

Her relationship with Arthur ‘Boy’ Capel, another wealthy man, proved even more pivotal. Capel financed her first shops and his style influenced her designs. The design of Chanel No. 5’s bottle is believed to be inspired by items he possessed. Their nine-year affair ended with his death in 1919, an event that deeply affected Chanel.  She opened boutiques in Deauville in 1913 and Biarritz in 1915, introducing casual clothing made from previously unconventional materials like jersey.  These ventures proved successful, and in 1919, she established her couture house at 31 rue Cambon in Paris.

Throughout her career, Chanel cultivated relationships with prominent figures in the arts and aristocracy. She supported the Ballets Russes, financially backing productions and designing costumes. She also formed a close friendship with Misia Sert and had a brief affair with Igor Stravinsky.  Her association with Vera Bate Lombardi led to connections with British aristocracy, including an extended affair with the Duke of Westminster, who showered her with gifts and further solidified her social standing.  However, the Duke’s antisemitism seemingly reinforced existing prejudices within Chanel. Later in life, Chanel struggled with morphine addiction and was known for her sharp wit and sometimes destructive personality. She spent decades attempting to regain full control of her perfume business, Parfums Chanel, which she’d initially licensed to the Wertheimer brothers.

title: Jacques Cousteau
text:
Jacques-Yves Cousteau, born in France in 1910 and passing away in 1997, was a multifaceted figure renowned as a naval officer, oceanographer, filmmaker, and author. He is best known for co-inventing the Aqua-Lung, the first successful open-circuit self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, which revolutionized underwater exploration and enabled him to create groundbreaking underwater documentaries. Cousteau’s passion for the ocean developed after an automobile accident curtailed his ambitions of becoming a naval pilot.

Throughout his career, Cousteau dedicated himself to exploring and documenting the underwater world. His first book, *The Silent World*, published in 1953, detailed his undersea discoveries and notably surmised the existence of echolocation in porpoises. This book was later adapted into a critically acclaimed documentary film of the same name, co-directed with Louis Malle. *The Silent World* film won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival in 1956, a distinction it held as the only documentary to do so for nearly fifty years, and also received the Academy Award for Best Documentary in 1957. 

Cousteau further shared his explorations through television, hosting *The Undersea World of Jacques Cousteau* from 1966 to 1976, and *The Cousteau Odyssey* from 1977 to 1982. These series brought the mysteries of the ocean into homes worldwide. Early underwater experiments took place in Toulon, aided by a friend lending him early swimming goggles. Later, during World War II, Cousteau and Marcel Ichac collaborated on underwater films, including *Par dix-huit mètres de fond* and *Épaves*, utilizing early Aqua-Lung prototypes developed with Émile Gagnan. During this period, he also aided the French Navy, and was involved in a commando operation against Italian espionage services.

After the war, Cousteau established the GERS (Underwater Studies and Research Group) of the French Navy. He continued to refine the Aqua-Lung, making extended underwater exploration possible. He embarked on numerous expeditions, including archaeological work in the Mediterranean, with the *Élie Monnier*, and later, with the research vessel *Calypso*, which he leased for a symbolic one franc a year. These voyages led to discoveries such as the wrecks of the HMHS *Britannic* and the French ship *La Therese*. 

Cousteau’s commitment to ocean conservation led to the creation of the Cousteau Society for the Protection of Ocean Life in 1973. Throughout his life, he received numerous accolades, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom and election to the Académie française. He was involved in projects like the Conshelf underwater habitats, aiming to allow humans to live and work on the seafloor. His later years were marked by personal tragedy with the loss of his son, Philippe, in a plane crash in 1979, and his wife Simone to cancer in 1990, after which he remarried.  Jacques-Yves Cousteau ultimately left a lasting legacy as a pioneering explorer and advocate for marine conservation.

title: Ana Cláudia Bolzan
text:
Ana Cláudia Bolzan e Silva, born on July 15, 1996, is a professional handball player representing both Sport Lisboa e Benfica and the Brazilian national handball team. Her primary position is left wing. While the article provides limited biographical detail, it highlights her accomplishments within the sport at both the club and international levels.

Bolzan has achieved success in club competitions, notably winning the Pan American Women's Club Handball Championship in 2017. This victory demonstrates her skill and contribution to a winning team on a continental scale. More recently, in 2022, she again demonstrated her competitive prowess by securing another championship title, this time at the South and Central American Women's Club Handball Championship. 

Her performance in the 2022 South and Central American Women's Club Handball Championship was particularly recognized. Beyond the team’s overall win, Bolzan was individually honored with selection to the All-Star team as the left wing, acknowledging her as one of the top players in that position throughout the tournament. This award signifies her consistently high level of play and impact on the game.

The article also points to Bolzan’s participation in major international events. Links are provided to profiles on the International Handball Federation website, Olympedia, and Olympics.com, and the Paris 2024 Summer Olympics website, indicating her involvement and recognition within the Olympic movement. The inclusion of a link to her Instagram profile suggests a degree of public profile and engagement. 

Although specific details about her career trajectory or personal life are not included in this brief overview, the provided information firmly establishes Ana Cláudia Bolzan e Silva as a significant figure in Brazilian handball, with a track record of success at both the club and potentially international level, and with ongoing participation in high-profile competitions such as the Olympics. Her achievements demonstrate a dedication to the sport and a consistent ability to perform at a high level, earning her both team victories and individual accolades.

title: Aditya Kalyanpur
text:
Aditya Kalyanpur, born in Mumbai, India on July 21, 1978, is a highly accomplished Tabla player rooted in the traditions of the Punjab gharana. He began his intensive musical training at the exceptionally young age of five, receiving tutelage from two of the most respected figures in Tabla performance: the late Alla Rakha Khan and his son, the renowned Zakir Hussain. Despite his dedication to music, Kalyanpur also pursued formal education, graduating with a commerce degree from Mithibai College.

Kalyanpur first gained public recognition at the age of eleven with a notable performance alongside his guru, Zakir Hussain, in the commercial for “Wah Taj!”. This early exposure marked the beginning of a distinguished career characterized by a distinctive playing style. His technique is described as possessing a bold and clear articulation of rhythmic syllables, combined with remarkable precision and a vast collection of compositions. He is also known for his improvisational skills.

Throughout his career, Kalyanpur has collaborated with a truly impressive array of prominent musicians across various genres. He has frequently accompanied masters of Hindustani classical music, including Shivkumar Sharma, Amjad Ali Khan, Prabha Atre, N. Rajam, Sultan Khan, Shahid Parvez, Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, Satish Vyas, Shujaat Khan, and Nayan Ghosh. Demonstrating his versatility, he has also performed with leading figures in Carnatic music such as T. N. Krishnan, N. Ramani, U. Shrinivas, and Lalgudi Krishnan. 

His reach extends beyond the realm of classical Indian music. Kalyanpur joined A.R. Rahman on the “JAI HO World Tour!” and has contributed to popular Western music, appearing on Katy Perry’s song “Legendary Lovers” from her album *Prism*. He has also recorded with Keith Richards, the guitarist from The Rolling Stones, showcasing his ability to seamlessly integrate into diverse musical settings.

Kalyanpur’s accomplishments have been recognized with numerous awards and accolades. He is a “TOP” Grade Artist of All India Radio, and has received the ‘Taal – Mani’ award from the Sur Singar Samiti. He is also a recipient of the Vidyasagar Award from ITC, and holds the title of Sangeet Visharad. He was granted a National Scholarship for Advanced Training by the Government of India, and was an awardee of the Pandit Jasraj Competition hosted by the Vedic Heritage Center in Long Island, New York. 

His performances have taken him to international stages, including appearances at the Orient Arts Festival in Estonia, the Edinburgh Festival in Scotland (2003), the Earagal Arts Festival in Ireland, Jazz Yatra in Mumbai, the Great Lakes Folk Festival in Lansing, Michigan, and the Saptak Festival.

title: Jamie Dornan
text:
Jamie Dornan is a Northern Irish actor, model, and musician who has garnered recognition with two Irish Film and Television Awards and nominations for a BAFTA Television Award and a Golden Globe Award. Born in 1982, he began his career as a model in 2001, quickly gaining attention and being dubbed “the Golden Torso” by *The New York Times*, and later being named one of the “25 Biggest Male Models of All Time” by *Vogue*. Prior to acting, he was also a member of the folk band Sons of Jim, releasing music until 2008.

Dornan’s acting debut came in 2006 with a role in Sofia Coppola’s *Marie Antoinette*. He followed this with smaller parts in independent films and television, including a recurring role in *Once Upon a Time* from 2011 to 2013. A breakthrough came with his portrayal of serial killer Paul Spector in the crime drama *The Fall* (2013-2016), earning him critical acclaim and a BAFTA nomination. This role significantly broadened his professional opportunities.

He gained international prominence playing Christian Grey in the *Fifty Shades* film trilogy (2015-2018), which, despite critical panning, proved a commercial success, grossing $1.32 billion. Dornan has stated the franchise opened doors for other roles he desired. Subsequent film work includes appearances in *Anthropoid* (2016), *Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar* (2021), and *Belfast* (2021), for which he received a Golden Globe nomination. He also starred as the lead in the thriller drama *The Tourist* (2022-2024).

Dornan’s personal life has been marked by loss, with his mother passing away when he was 16 and his father succumbing to COVID-19 complications in 2021. He credits his father with consistent support throughout his career. He has two older sisters, one working at Disney in London and the other a fashion designer. He attended Methodist College Belfast, where he participated in rugby and the drama department, laying the groundwork for his later career. He briefly attended Teesside University before moving to London to pursue acting training, although he never formally enrolled in drama school. 

Throughout his modelling career, he worked with prominent fashion houses like Dior Homme, Hugo Boss, and Calvin Klein, appearing in numerous advertising campaigns and collaborating with renowned photographers. While successful as a model, he initially hesitated to embrace the profession, but was encouraged by his sisters. He has consistently returned to modelling, becoming a global brand ambassador for Loewe in 2024. His recent film roles include *Heart of Stone* (2023) and *A Haunting in Venice* (2023), continuing to demonstrate his versatility as an actor. In 2020, *The Irish Times* recognized him as one of Ireland’s greatest film actors.

title: Billy Snedden
text:
Billy Snedden was born in Perth, Western Australia, in 1926, the youngest of six children to Scottish immigrant parents. His father worked as a stonemason and had a somewhat troubled past, and the family moved to Perth after a fire destroyed their home in a mining town. Snedden’s early life was marked by his father’s absence and the need for family members to contribute to the household income. He attended local schools and began working part-time from a young age, displaying an aptitude for sport as well. He briefly attended university before enlisting in the Royal Australian Air Force in 1945, though his service coincided with the end of World War II and involved mainly non-combat duties.

Following the war, Snedden completed his law degree at the University of Western Australia and began practicing law. He became involved in the Young Liberals, eventually becoming its federal chairman. He then worked for the Department of Immigration, serving in Italy and England, gaining fluency in Italian during his time abroad. Returning to Australia in 1955, he moved to Melbourne and successfully entered Federal Parliament as the member for Bruce.

Snedden steadily rose through the ranks of the Liberal Party, holding various ministerial portfolios under multiple Prime Ministers from 1964 to 1972, including Attorney-General, Minister for Immigration, Minister for Labour and National Service, and finally Treasurer. He became Deputy Leader in 1971. Following the Liberal Party’s defeat in the 1972 election, he assumed the leadership, promising a more liberal approach. However, his leadership was fraught with challenges, notably his controversial decision to block the Labor government’s budget in 1974, leading to a double dissolution election. 

Despite campaigning on the slogan "Oh no, not Snedden!", Whitlam was re-elected. Snedden faced internal challenges from Malcolm Fraser, eventually losing the leadership in 1975. He then surprised many by accepting the position of Speaker of the House of Representatives in 1976, a role he held until his retirement from Parliament in 1983. As Speaker, he championed parliamentary independence and sought to restore dignity to the office, even reinstating the traditional wig and gown. 

After leaving Parliament, Snedden remained active in public life, serving as chairman of the Melbourne Football Club and on the board of the Victorian Football League. His death in 1987 was notable due to the unusual circumstances surrounding it, involving the ex-girlfriend of his son. Throughout his career, Snedden was known for his pragmatism and commitment to parliamentary procedure, leaving a significant mark on Australian political life.

title: Lali Espósito
text:
Mariana “Lali” Espósito, born in Buenos Aires in 1991, is a multi-talented Argentine artist working as a singer, actress, dancer, and model. Her career began in 2003 with a role in the children’s telenovela *Rincón de Luz*, followed by supporting parts in popular series like *Floricienta* and *Chiquititas*. She achieved widespread fame with her leading role in *Casi Ángeles*, which propelled her to recognition throughout Latin America, the Middle East, and Europe. This success led to her becoming a member of the teen pop band Teen Angels from 2007 to 2012, touring extensively with the group.

In 2014, Espósito launched her solo music career by signing with Sony Music Argentina and releasing her debut album, *A Bailar*, a pop and EDM-influenced record that spawned hit singles like “Asesina,” “Mil Años Luz,” and “Histeria.” Both *A Bailar* and her subsequent albums, *Soy* (2016) and *Brava* (2018), were certified gold in Argentina. *Soy* featured the singles “Soy,” “Boomerang,” and “Ego,” while *Brava* included “Una Na,” “Tu Novia,” and “100 Grados.” Her fourth studio album, *Libra*, was released in 2020 with singles “Laligera”, “Como Así” and “Lo Que Tengo Yo”. 

Alongside her musical pursuits, Espósito has continued to build a successful acting career. She garnered critical praise for her stage performance as Abigail Williams in *The Crucible* and for her roles in the crime thriller *The Accused* and the Netflix action series *Sky Rojo*. She has starred in several telenovelas including *Solamente vos* and *Esperanza mía*. 

Throughout her career, Espósito has accumulated numerous awards and nominations. These include six Gardel Awards, five MTV Europe Music Awards, thirteen Argentina Kids' Choice Awards, a Billboard Latin Music Award, and seven MTV Millennial Awards. She has also been nominated for the Lo Nuestro Awards and the Seoul International Drama Awards. In 2015, *Infobae* recognized her as one of the ten most influential women in Argentina.

Born into a family with connections to the entertainment industry – her mother manages her tours, and her siblings work as a makeup artist and former athlete – Espósito’s early life included a childhood appearance on the television program *Caramelito y Vos*. She inadvertently auditioned for Cris Morena, leading to her role in *Rincón de Luz*.  She has since become a prominent figure in Latin American entertainment, consistently achieving commercial success and critical acclaim in both her music and acting endeavors.

title: Rui Campos
text:
Rui Campos, also known simply as Rui, was a Brazilian footballer who lived from August 2nd, 1922, to January 2nd, 2002. He is best known for his participation in the Brazil national team during the 1950 FIFA World Cup. Born in São Paulo, Rui enjoyed a professional club career spanning several prominent Brazilian clubs. 

Throughout his career, he played for Bonsucesso, Fluminense, Bangu, São Paulo, and Palmeiras. His time with São Paulo Football Club proved particularly successful, where he established a strong and effective midfield partnership alongside fellow players José Carlos Bauer and Alfredo Noronha. The article highlights this trio’s contribution to the team’s achievements.

Rui’s involvement with the Brazil national team was substantial, accumulating a total of 30 appearances between 1944 and 1950. This period included his selection for and participation in the 1950 FIFA World Cup, a momentous tournament for Brazilian football, and one remembered for its dramatic conclusion. 

Beyond the World Cup, Rui Campos also achieved international success with Brazil by being a part of the team that won the Copa América in 1949. However, his World Cup experience ended in disappointment as Brazil finished as runners-up in the 1950 tournament. While the article does not detail his specific role or performance in these matches, it establishes his presence as a key member of the national squad during this era.

His accomplishments were recognized through several team honours. During his time at São Paulo, he was part of the squads that won the Campeonato Paulista – the São Paulo State Championship – in four separate years: 1945, 1946, 1948, and 1949. These victories cemented his legacy within the club’s history. Combined with his Copa América win with the national team and participation in the 1950 World Cup, Rui Campos had a decorated career representing both club and country.

title: Nonzee Nimibutr
text:
Nonzee Nimibutr, born December 18, 1962, is a prominent Thai filmmaker working as a director, producer, and screenwriter. He is considered a leading figure in the “New Wave” of Thai cinema, alongside directors like Pen-Ek Ratanaruang, Wisit Sasanatieng, and Apichatpong Weerasethakul. His family has connections to Thai media history through his relative, Lieutenant General Phachoen Nimitbutr, who founded Thailand’s first television station.

Nonzee began his career directing television commercials and music videos before making his feature film debut in 1997 with *Dang Bireley's and Young Gangsters*, a crime film influenced by John Woo, which won Best Picture at the Thailand National Film Awards and received a nomination at the Vancouver International Film Festival. He quickly followed this success with *Nang Nak* (1999), a ghost thriller based on a well-known Thai folk tale, also garnering Best Picture at the Thailand National Film Awards. These two films are credited with revitalizing the Thai film industry.

He then pioneered a trend of pan-Asian film production with *Jan Dara* (2001), featuring a Hong Kong actress and seeking funding from international studios. *Jan Dara* sparked controversy due to its mature themes of incest, rape, and abortion, requiring censorship cuts for its release in Thailand.  Nonzee expanded his role in the industry by becoming a prolific producer, lending his name to films such as *Bangkok Dangerous*, *Tears of the Black Tiger*, *Bang Rajan*, and *Monrak Transistor*. He co-founded the production company Cinemasia with Duangkamol Limcharoen, who sadly passed away in 2003.

Continuing his pan-Asian approach, he participated in the horror anthology *Three* (2002), directing a segment alongside directors from Hong Kong and Korea.  His later directorial work includes *OK Baytong* (2003), a drama set in Southern Thailand addressing themes of religious and political conflict, and the short film *The Ceiling* (2005) for the Asian Film Academy. He also directed *Queens of Langkasuka* (2008), a historical-fantasy epic, and has been involved in developing projects like *Toyol*, a Singaporean co-production, and a live-action adaptation of the comic *Noo Hin: The Movie*.

Throughout his career, Nonzee has continued to produce films, including *The Letter* and *The Eye 2*. In 2008, he was recognized for his contributions to Thai cinema with the Thailand Culture Ministry's Silpathorn Award, joining a prestigious group of fellow filmmakers. His recent work includes *Distortion* (2012), *Timeline* (2015), *The Gift* (2017) and *Once Upon A Star* (2023), a Netflix film.

title: Albert Outler
text:
Albert Cook Outler was a prominent 20th-century American Methodist historian, theologian, and pastor, born in Georgia in 1908 and passing away in 1989. He dedicated his life to scholarship and ministry, serving as a professor at Duke University, Yale University, and most notably, Southern Methodist University, where he held a long-term position. His academic work encompassed Christian history, theology, doctrine, and specifically, Wesleyan studies. 

Outler was a significant figure in the ecumenical movement, actively participating in efforts towards Christian unity. He served as a delegate to the Consultation on Church Union and held a position on the Faith & Order board of the World Council of Churches. He also acted as an official observer representing the Methodist tradition at the Second Vatican Council. Along with colleagues like Colin Williams, Frank Baker, and John Deschner, Outler’s scholarship played a vital role in revitalizing contemporary study of John Wesley and establishing Wesley as a significant theological voice. He authored *John Wesley* for "The Library of Protestant Thought" series, a groundbreaking work that positioned Wesley within the broader Western theological tradition, and produced critical editions of Wesley’s Sermons.

A cornerstone of Outler’s theological contribution was his articulation of the “Wesleyan Quadrilateral” – scripture, tradition, reason, and personal experience – as the method by which Wesley approached theology. This framework became central to Methodist understanding, particularly within the United Methodist Church, and informed the theological statement adopted by the newly formed church in 1968. He is credited with uniquely emphasizing the importance of “Tradition” within this Wesleyan system. His focus on early church history and thought also resonated with the paleo-orthodox movement and contemporary evangelicalism, influencing figures like Thomas C. Oden. 

Outler was a prolific writer, producing books and articles not only on Methodist history and theology but also on patrology, psychotherapy, and general theology. His extensive body of work has been compiled into the Albert Outler Library series. His published books range from explorations of Clement of Alexandria and Augustine to analyses of Vatican II and the unity of Christians. He also contributed articles to publications like *The Christian Century* and *Perkins School of Theology Journal*. Resources relating to his life and work, including archival papers, are available online, and some of his writings have been made accessible through LibriVox as public domain audiobooks.

title: Uee
text:
Kim Yu-jin, known professionally as Uee, was born on April 9, 1988, in Daejeon, South Korea. She initially aimed for an acting career but debuted as a singer, joining the girl group Five Girls in 2007. This group disbanded shortly after formation due to financial difficulties within their agency. Before her breakthrough, she gained public attention as “Mok-dong Girl” after being filmed at her baseball player father’s game, and later for her resemblance to actress Moon Geun-young.

Uee officially debuted as a member of the popular girl group After School in 2009. Simultaneously, she began her acting career with a role in the historical drama *Queen Seondeok*, which proved successful. She quickly gained recognition, also appearing in *You’re Beautiful* and as part of the project group 4Tomorrow. Her popularity continued with roles in dramas like *Birdie Buddy* and *Ojakgyo Family* in 2011, the latter earning her Best New Actress awards. She also released her first solo single, “Sok Sok Sok,” and became a co-host on the variety show *Night After Night*.

Throughout the early to mid-2010s, Uee balanced her music and acting careers. She hosted the music show *Music Bank* and took on leading roles in *Jeon Woo-chi*, *Golden Rainbow*, and *Hogu’s Love*. She participated in survival shows *Law of the Jungle* and *Barefooted Friends*, even co-writing and performing the song "Hero" for the latter. While enjoying success, she expressed a desire to be recognized solely for her acting skill and to move away from being labelled an “idol-turned-actor.”

In 2017, Uee left After School after eight years and signed with a new agency. She continued to pursue acting, with roles in *Manhole*, *My Contracted Husband, Mr. Oh*, and *My Only One*. She then signed with King Entertainment, followed by Lucky Company, appearing in shows like *Cabin Crew Season 2* and *I Live Alone*, showcasing her everyday life. She also hosted the 2020 Live in DMZ Concert and currently hosts the fitness program *Last Fit with U-ie*. 

Uee has been open about facing criticism regarding her weight and online harassment, with her agency taking legal action against malicious commenters in 2018. She has also dated actors Lee Sang-yoon and Kangnam, though both relationships ended after a period of time. Beyond her entertainment career, Uee demonstrated her philanthropic side with a significant donation to support young women’s hygiene and well-being in 2022.

title: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
text:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known simply as Lula, is a Brazilian politician and former trade unionist who currently serves as the 39th president of Brazil, a position he previously held from 2003 to 2011. Born in 1945 in Pernambuco, Lula experienced a difficult childhood marked by poverty and limited education, not learning to read until age ten. He began working at a young age, eventually becoming a metalworker and a prominent trade union leader, leading strikes in the ABC region during Brazil’s military dictatorship. He was a key figure in the movement for Brazil’s redemocratization, helping found the Workers’ Party (PT) in 1980 and participating in the Diretas Já campaign for direct elections.

Lula ran for president multiple times, unsuccessfully in 1989, 1994, and 1998, before finally winning in 2002 and being re-elected in 2006. His presidencies coincided with a period of economic growth in South America, and he implemented social welfare programs like Bolsa Família, contributing to a reduction in poverty and external debt. He also engaged in foreign policy initiatives, focusing on regional integration and global trade. Despite his popularity, his first terms were shadowed by corruption scandals, including the Mensalão vote-buying affair.

Following his second term, Lula remained active in politics. However, in 2017, he was convicted on charges of money laundering and corruption as part of the Operation Car Wash investigation, leading to 580 days in prison. He was disqualified from running in the 2018 presidential election.  Further convictions followed in 2019, but in 2021, the Supreme Federal Court annulled his convictions, citing procedural errors and bias. 

Legally able to run again, Lula campaigned in 2022 and defeated incumbent Jair Bolsonaro in a runoff election. He was inaugurated in January 2023 as the oldest person to assume the Brazilian presidency and the first to win a third non-consecutive term, and the first to defeat an incumbent president.

Lula’s early life was characterized by hardship; his family moved to São Paulo in search of better opportunities, but faced financial struggles and family division. He worked various jobs from a young age, including street vending and as a shoeshiner, before securing a position in a metallurgical company where he later suffered an accident that cost him a finger. This experience fuelled his involvement in union activities. Inspired by his brother’s political leanings, he rose through the ranks of the labor movement, becoming president of the Steel Workers' Union.

Throughout his political career, Lula has been described as left-wing. As president, he oversaw the implementation of social programs aimed at reducing hunger and poverty, like the expansion of Bolsa Escola into Bolsa Família. He also launched initiatives focused on education, housing, and infrastructure. His economic policies benefited from a boom in commodity prices, allowing for debt reduction and investment in social programs. While his presidency saw economic progress, it also faced criticism regarding the slow pace of educational improvements and the challenges of implementing social programs effectively.

title: Blanca Errázuriz
text:
Blanca Elena Errázuriz Vergara, later known as Bianca de Saulles, lived a dramatic life marked by wealth, scandal, and ultimately, tragedy. Born in 1894 in Viña del Mar, Chile, she came from the prominent and politically connected Errázuriz family. Her early life included education at a convent in London, following the death of her mining magnate father when she was just two years old. In 1911, at the age of sixteen, she married John de Saulles, an American businessman fifteen years her senior, after overcoming some initial family objections due to their age and religious differences. They married in France after a ceremony in Paris, having previously lived in New York City.

The couple had one son, John “Jack” de Saulles, in 1912, but their marriage quickly deteriorated due to de Saulles’ infidelities. Blanca filed for divorce in 1916, during which time she befriended Rudolph Valentino, who provided testimony supporting her claims of her husband’s adultery. De Saulles responded by attempting to discredit Valentino, resulting in the actor's arrest on dubious charges and a damaging scandal that impacted his career. Blanca, however, did not offer Valentino gratitude for his support, and ended their association.

Following the divorce finalized in December 1916, a confrontation with her ex-husband led to a fatal shooting. On August 3, 1917, Blanca drove to de Saulles’ home and, after an argument over custody of their son – despite a court ruling in her favor – shot him five times when he attempted to disarm her. She surrendered to police and was charged with first-degree murder. The ensuing trial was a sensation, with Blanca defended by Henry Uterhart and her maid, Suzanne Monteau, providing key testimony. She gained public sympathy, championed by suffragettes who viewed her as a victim of societal chauvinism. 

Ultimately, Blanca Errázuriz was acquitted of all charges in December 1917 by a unanimous “popular” verdict. After the trial, she moved to San Francisco, secured full custody of her son, and eventually returned with him to Chile. She remarried in 1921 to engineer Fernando Santa Cruz Wilson, but they later divorced. In her later years, she became estranged from her son, Jack Jr., who moved to the United States. Suffering from poor health, she died by suicide in 1940 in Viña del Mar, having taken an overdose of barbiturates. Her story inspired the 1918 silent film "The Woman and the Law”, though names were altered for the adaptation. Her brother, Guillermo Errázuriz, also tragically took his own life in 1922 following a heartbreak involving actress Peggy Hopkins Joyce.

title: Annie Landouw
text:
Annie Landouw, born in Surakarta, Central Java in 1913, was a prominent Indonesian singer and actress best known for her work in the keroncong genre. Her early life was marked by a childhood illness that resulted in the loss of her sight. Following this, she was adopted by her aunt and uncle. Her musical talent emerged in 1927 when she won a singing competition, a Concours concert held at a night fair in Surakarta. This victory led to a recording contract with Beka, prompting her move to Batavia, now Jakarta, where she rapidly gained recognition and popularity.

Landouw’s career progressed quickly, and by 1938 she had become a member of the NIROM radio troupe, performing keroncong music. The following year, she joined Hugo Dumas' Lief Java troupe, further cementing her position in the entertainment world. Concurrent with her radio work, Landouw began contributing to the burgeoning Indonesian film industry. She initially provided vocals for films produced by Tan's Film, beginning with *Fatima* in 1938 and continuing with *Gagak Item* (Black Raven) in 1939. Later in 1939, she made her acting debut in the film *Siti Akbari*. She then appeared in two more films in 1940: *Sorga Ka Toedjoe* (Seventh Heaven) and *Roekihati*.

Landouw’s skill as a keroncong singer brought her widespread fame and a dedicated fan base. In 1940, arrangements were made for eye surgery to potentially restore her sight. Her admirers organized a fundraising effort to assist with the costs, but Landouw ultimately declined their charitable offers. 

After Indonesia achieved independence, Landouw continued to pursue her singing career, but did not appear in any further films. She passed away on August 17, 1982. Her impact on Indonesian culture extends beyond her recordings and performances. Music scholar Peter Keppy has proposed a potential connection between Landouw’s success and a character in Armijn Pane’s 1940 novel *Belenggu*. Keppy suggests that the character of Yah, a famous keroncong singer known as Siti Hayati within the novel, may have been influenced by Landouw’s popularity and persona.

title: Danny Almonte
text:
Danny Almonte Rojas, born in Moca, Dominican Republic on April 7, 1987, became a baseball sensation in 2001 as a Little League pitcher for a team from the Bronx, New York. He quickly gained attention for his fastball, reaching speeds of 76 mph – equivalent to a 102 mph major league pitch – and earned the nickname “Little Unit” due to his resemblance to Randy Johnson. Almonte led his team, nicknamed the “Baby Bombers,” to a third-place finish in the 2001 Little League World Series, highlighted by a perfect game against Florida. They were celebrated with honors from the New York Yankees and the city of New York.

However, questions arose regarding Almonte’s age, fueled by his size and pitching prowess. Rumors circulated that he was older than the Little League age limit of 12. Investigations by other teams and Little League officials initially found no evidence of wrongdoing, with league president Rolando Paulino vehemently defending Almonte’s birthdate. The truth emerged when *Sports Illustrated* reporters discovered a birth certificate in Moca registering Almonte’s birth in 1987, meaning he was 14 during the 2001 series. This contradicted a later-registered birth certificate claiming a 1989 birthdate, which his mother maintained was accurate.

Further investigation revealed that witnesses associated with the 1989 birth certificate denied its validity. Dominican officials ultimately confirmed Almonte’s 1987 birthdate. As a result, the Baby Bombers were forced to forfeit their wins, and Almonte was declared ineligible. His father, Felipe, was banned from Little League competition for life, and Paulino also received a lifetime ban due to his responsibility for player eligibility. Criminal charges were filed against Felipe for falsifying the birth certificate, though Danny was cleared of any wrongdoing, having been unaware of the deception.

Following the scandal, Almonte remained in New York, becoming the ward of Rolando Paulino. He continued to play baseball, appearing in a championship game for Public Schools Athletic League in 2004. He briefly played for the Southern Illinois Miners in the Frontier League in 2007, but was released after six appearances. He then attended and excelled at Western Oklahoma State College, demonstrating skill as both a pitcher and a hitter. A sore arm eventually forced him to abandon pitching, and he transitioned to playing outfield in semi-pro leagues. By 2010, he was working as a volunteer assistant baseball coach at his high school in the Bronx, acknowledging his professional baseball aspirations had diminished. 

In 2006, Almonte married Rosy Perdomo, who was 30 at the time of their wedding, when Almonte was 18. Throughout the ordeal and beyond, the controversy surrounding his age significantly impacted his baseball career and public image.

title: Trevor Noah
text:
Trevor Noah, born in Johannesburg, South Africa on February 20, 1984, is a multi-talented entertainer working as a comedian, writer, producer, political commentator, actor, and television host. He is best known as the former host of *The Daily Show* on Comedy Central, a position he held from 2015 to 2022, earning him two Primetime Emmy Awards and recognition as a prominent figure in New York media and globally.

Noah’s early life was shaped by the apartheid laws in South Africa. His father is Swiss-German and his mother, Patricia, is Xhosa. Because of apartheid, his parents’ relationship was illegal at the time of his birth, and he was classified as “Coloured.” He was raised by his mother and grandmother in Soweto. He was educated at Maryvale College and grew up in a household that blended Christian beliefs with exposure to Jewish traditions through his mother’s conversion.

He began his career in South Africa in 2008, taking on various hosting roles with the South African Broadcasting Corporation and appearing as a contestant on *Strictly Come Dancing*. He also created and hosted his own late-night talk show, *Tonight with Trevor Noah*, from 2010 to 2011. His breakthrough came in 2014 when he became a Senior International Correspondent for *The Daily Show*, ultimately leading to his succession of Jon Stewart as host in 2015.

Beyond television, Noah is a published author, releasing his autobiographical comedy book *Born a Crime* in 2016, which became a New York Times Bestseller. He has also been a frequent host of major events, including the Grammy Awards from 2021-2025 and the 2022 White House Correspondents Dinner.

Throughout his career, Noah’s comedy often draws from his unique upbringing and observations on race and culture. He gained recognition performing at comedy clubs in South Africa and later in the United States, appearing on shows like *The Tonight Show* and *Late Show with David Letterman*. He has faced some controversy over past jokes that were deemed insensitive. 

Following his departure from *The Daily Show* in December 2022, Noah has continued to pursue various projects, including hosting the Grammy Awards, launching a Spotify podcast titled *What Now? with Trevor Noah*, and acting in films. He has cited comedians like Richard Pryor, Eddie Murphy, Chris Rock, and Dave Chappelle as major influences, as well as his predecessor, Jon Stewart, whom he views as a mentor. He currently resides in New York City and speaks multiple languages. His mother’s resilience, marked by surviving a shooting incident by her former husband, is a significant theme in his life and work.

title: Thomas Jack
text:
Thomas Jack, born Tom Jack Johnston, is an Australian DJ, record producer, and musician who is credited with popularizing and even coining the term “tropical house” in 2013. He grew up on a large dairy farm in rural New South Wales, working with thousands of cows before moving to Sydney to study music production. His initial foray into music production began with the PlayStation game eJay, before progressing to Ableton software, a gift from his father. Prior to achieving success, he experimented with various stage names including Dirty-D and Tom Foolery.

Johnston’s musical style, which he describes as summery and laid-back dance music, blends deep house with influences from acoustic rock and jam bands. His tracks frequently incorporate live instrumentation such as saxophone, flute, piano, and guitar, aiming for an uplifting and relaxed atmosphere, and often include sampled speeches. He initially worried about being pigeonholed by the “tropical house” label, wanting to maintain artistic freedom.

His career gained momentum after being discovered on SoundCloud by Myles Shear, who brought him to Miami. He launched a popular podcast mix series called *Tropical House*, featuring mixes from artists like Felix Jaehn and Robin Schulz. He became known for original tracks like "Symphony" and "The Final Speech," alongside remixes of artists such as Of Monsters & Men and OneRepublic. Extensive touring followed, leading him to spend significant time in the United States, particularly Florida.

In 2015, Johnston participated in the *We Are Your Friends* movie tour and launched the *Tropical Express Tour* with artists including Bag Raiders and Felix Jaehn. He released his debut single, "Rivers," featuring Nico & Vinz, which achieved chart success in Belgium, the Netherlands, and Norway, accompanied by a music video on his YouTube channel. He also expressed intentions to potentially launch a tropical house record label, though he prioritized completing his debut album. 

He released a second single, "Rise Up" with Jasmine Thompson in 2016, peaking at fourteenth in Belgium, and also had an accompanying music video released on Thompson’s YouTube channel. Though he planned to release an album in 2016, a busy touring schedule delayed production. 

Johnston’s influence extends beyond his own music; he inadvertently popularized the “tropical house” genre, which was then embraced by artists like Kygo and Klingande. He played a role in launching the careers of both Kygo and Klingande by introducing them to his manager, Myles Shear. He remains interested in the evolution of the genre, hoping to see it progress and avoid becoming overly commercialized, while also maintaining his own artistic identity.

title: Akbar Hossain
text:
Akbar Hossain, born on January 18, 1941, in Kashari Patty, Comilla District, was a prominent Bangladeshi politician and a decorated military officer. He served multiple terms as a government minister, holding portfolios including Shipping, Environment and Forests, and Petroleum and Mineral Resources, and was a long-standing figure within the Bangladesh National Party (BNP).

Hossain began his career in the military, joining the Kakul Military Academy in Pakistan in May 1966. He was commissioned into the 31 Baluch Regiment and simultaneously pursued a bachelor’s degree at the University of Dhaka, which he completed in 1969. He actively participated in the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971, initially serving under Khaled Musharraf and later with Ziaur Rahman’s Z Force. His bravery and contributions during the war earned him the prestigious ‘Bir Protik’ award for gallantry. He voluntarily retired from the Bangladesh Army in December 1973, having reached the rank of lieutenant colonel.

Transitioning to politics, Hossain became involved in the formation of the United People’s Party (UPP) in January 1974 and rose to the position of its vice-president. He later left the UPP when it merged with the Jatiyatabadi Front, and became a founding member of the Bangladesh National Party (BNP). Within the BNP, he held several key positions, starting as special secretary, progressing to joint secretary general, and ultimately serving as one of the party’s vice-presidents until his death. 

His political career included a significant period of ministerial service. He first entered the government in 1978 as Minister for Petroleum and Mineral Resources under President Ziaur Rahman. He was first elected to the Bangladesh Parliament in 1979, representing the Comilla 8th constituency, and successfully defended this seat in four subsequent elections. During the period of military rule under General Hossain Mohammad Ershad, Hossain faced political opposition and was imprisoned five times. 

Following the end of the military dictatorship and the election of Khaleda Zia as Prime Minister, Akbar Hossain was appointed Minister for the Environment and Forests in October 1993. He again held a ministerial position after the BNP’s victory in the 8th Jatiyo Sangshad elections in October 2001, becoming Minister for Shipping in Khaleda Zia’s third term as Prime Minister. Akbar Hossain died in Dhaka on June 25, 2006, as a result of a heart attack.

title: Robbie Horgan
text:
Robbie Horgan, born on June 7, 1968, is a former Irish professional footballer who specialized as a goalkeeper. His professional career began with Shamrock Rovers, where he first appeared in a League of Ireland match on April 14, 1987. This game held particular significance as it was the final match played at Glenmalure Park (also known as Milltown) and determined the winner of the League of Ireland B Division, a title ultimately secured by Shamrock Rovers.

Horgan moved to Drogheda United in 1988, making his debut for the club on September 4th in a 2-1 victory against Bray Wanderers. He quickly established himself as a key player for Drogheda, achieving notable success during his time there. In the 1989 season, he maintained 12 clean sheets in 26 league matches, contributing to Drogheda United’s championship win in the League of Ireland First Division. He continued his strong form into the following season, 1990/1991, recording 15 clean sheets as Drogheda once again claimed the First Division title.

After spending four and a half years with Drogheda United at United Park, Horgan transferred to Shelbourne in November 1992. However, his time there was relatively brief, as he rejoined Shamrock Rovers in July 1994, remaining with the club for another eight years. During his second spell at Shamrock Rovers, Horgan gained European experience, playing in two UEFA Cup matches against Djurgårdens IF in the 2002–03 season. His final League of Ireland appearance as a player came at the end of the 2007 season.

Following his playing career, Horgan transitioned into coaching, serving as the goalkeeping coach at Sporting Fingal until the club ceased operations. In August 2009, he achieved a unique distinction, becoming the only player to have competed at both Milltown and Tallaght Stadium, marking a significant historical moment in Irish football.

Horgan returned to Drogheda United in February 2011, taking on the role of assistant to manager Mick Cooke. During their partnership, Drogheda United enjoyed success, winning the League of Ireland Cup in 2012. When Mick Cooke departed from Drogheda in November 2013, Horgan was promptly appointed as his replacement, stepping into the role of manager.

title: Ameyaw Debrah
text:
Ameyaw Debrah is a Ghanaian celebrity blogger, journalist, and reporter who is widely known for founding the entertainment website AmeyawDebrah.com. He earned a bachelor’s degree in publishing from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), where he was recognized as the Best Publishing Student in 2005. His career in media began during his time at Adisadel College, where he served as an editor for the school magazine in 1999.

After graduating from KNUST, Debrah completed his National Service Secretariat (NSS) program at Ovation International Magazine in Accra, focusing on coverage of the Ghanaian entertainment scene for an international audience. He then became a columnist for the Star newspaper before contributing to several pan-African websites – Jamati.com, Orijin-ent.com, and ModernGhana.com – in 2007. He also worked with the Netherlands-based media project Voices of Africa, providing content for Africanews.com.

In 2008, Debrah joined GhanaWeb.com as its entertainment editor and simultaneously launched his own blog, AmeyawDebrah.com. He eventually left Ghanaweb in 2012 to dedicate himself fully to his blog. He continues to contribute to other platforms, including the entertainment segment StarGist on Africa Magic, EbonyLife TV, and Glitz Africa Magazine. He has also served as an ambassador for the Malta Guinness Africa Rising Campaign. 

AmeyawDebrah.com gained traction with the help of a friend who assisted with hosting and domain acquisition. The site launched an iPhone app in 2010 and hosted an online talent competition in 2012 to promote emerging Ghanaian musicians, as well as the My Ghana Campaign, inviting video submissions on relevant national issues. 

Debrah’s career also includes leadership roles at Ringier Ghana, where he launched and managed Pulse Ghana in late 2014 before moving to Genesis Technology in 2015. He then served as editor-in-chief of Yen.com.gh from September 2015 to September 2017. Beyond journalism, he has worked in artist management, first with music producer Coptic, handling his affairs in Ghana and scouting talent for his Rebel Musik label, and later with Pappy Kojo in 2014.

In 2018, Debrah launched Ameyaw TV, a web portal showcasing various video formats, and subsequently debuted shows like Daily Buzz, News in One, and Trend Mill, with further programming planned. On a personal note, Ameyaw Debrah married Elsie Darkoa on March 6, 2018, and they have two sons: Nathan and Samuel Amo-Ameyaw, who plays for Southampton FC.

title: Balázs Bekő
text:
Balázs Bekő, born on December 15, 1971, is a Hungarian individual currently working as a football manager. He also has a background as a former professional football player, though the article does not detail his playing career. Currently, as of the information available, Bekő holds the position of head coach for the club Dorog.

Bekő’s managerial career has involved working with teams within the Hungarian football league system, specifically at the top tier level known as the Nemzeti Bajnokság I. His first documented head coaching role at this level began on June 24, 2013, when he was appointed to lead Kecskeméti TE. This marked a significant step in his career, placing him in charge of a club competing in Hungary’s highest football division.
