Following his time with Kecskeméti TE, Bekő continued to progress as a manager, securing another head coaching position within the Nemzeti Bajnokság I. This appointment came in the summer of 2015, when he became the head coach of Diósgyőri VTK. This move indicated sustained confidence in his abilities as a leader and tactician within Hungarian professional football. 

The information provided is limited in scope, focusing primarily on his managerial appointments. The article doesn’t delve into the specifics of his tactics, achievements, or the duration of his tenures with either Kecskeméti TE or Diósgyőri VTK. It simply establishes that he has held head coaching positions at clubs within the highest Hungarian league and currently manages Dorog. 

The source for this information is the official website of Diósgyőri VTK, suggesting that some of the details, particularly regarding his time with that club, originate directly from the team itself. The article is concise and functions as a brief biographical note, primarily identifying Bekő’s profession and highlighting key points in his managerial career to date. Beyond these points, no further details about his life or career are provided.

title: Jorge Enríquez
text:
Jorge Enríquez García, born on January 8, 1991, is a former Mexican professional footballer who played as a defensive midfielder. He is best known for being an Olympic gold medalist, a feat he achieved representing Mexico. His professional career began with C.D. Guadalajara, where he debuted on February 5, 2010, in a match against Pachuca CF, entering the game as a substitute for Adolfo Bautista during the Bicentenario tournament. He later scored his first professional goal in a quarter-final match against Monarcas Morelia, striking from outside the penalty area.

In December 2015, Enríquez was loaned from Guadalajara to Club León for a period of six months. Later in his career, in June 2018, he was transferred to the Cypriot club Omonia. 

Enríquez’s international career began with appearances for the Mexico national team at the 2011 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, where Mexico ultimately emerged victorious, securing qualification for the 2011 Pan American Games. He also participated in the 2011 Copa América with the U-22 Mexico squad, although they were eliminated in the group stage, finishing last in their group. 

He was a key player in the 2011 FIFA U-20 World Cup, where Mexico reached the semi-finals before being defeated by Brazil. They recovered to win the third-place match against France, and Enríquez was recognized for his performance, receiving the Bronze Ball award as the third-best player in the tournament. 

He further contributed to Mexico's success at the Pan American Games, winning a gold medal as a member of the team that defeated Argentina in the final. His most significant achievement came at the 2012 Summer Olympics, where he played a vital role in Mexico's journey to the gold medal, providing crucial passes and scoring the opening goal against Senegal in the quarter-finals. 

Throughout his career, Enríquez earned several accolades. With Guadalajara, he won the Copa MX Apertura in 2015. Representing Mexico’s youth teams, he won the 2011 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, the 2011 Pan American Games, the 2012 CONCACAF Olympic Qualifying Championship, and the Toulon Tournament in 2012, culminating in the Olympic gold medal later that year. His individual achievements include the FIFA U-20 World Cup Bronze Ball award in 2011. As of July 25, 2013, his international career statistics were recorded.

title: Wil Nieves
text:
Wil Nieves, born September 25, 1977, in Puerto Rico, enjoyed a lengthy professional baseball career primarily as a catcher, ultimately transitioning into a minor league coaching role. He played in Major League Baseball for seven different teams: the San Diego Padres, New York Yankees, Washington Nationals, Milwaukee Brewers, Colorado Rockies, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Philadelphia Phillies.

Nieves was initially drafted by the Padres in 1995 and debuted with them in 2002, appearing in 28 games. He was then selected off waivers by the Angels before being traded to the Yankees. With the Yankees in 2007, he served as a backup to Jorge Posada and was particularly valued as a personal catcher for pitcher Mike Mussina, assisting him through a difficult period. He even made a single appearance at first base due to a shortage of position players. Despite a brief, promising performance, he was designated for assignment and later played for the Yankees' Triple-A affiliate, Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, before becoming a free agent.

He continued his career with the Washington Nationals in 2008, where he hit his first major league home run – a walk-off against the Chicago Cubs. He filled a backup role for the Nationals in both 2009 and 2010, behind Jesus Flores and Iván Rodríguez respectively. Subsequent stints followed with the Milwaukee Brewers in 2010, the Atlanta Braves in 2011, and the Colorado Rockies in 2012. With the Rockies, he excelled in spring training, but was later called up to mentor younger players like Wilin Rosario and assist struggling pitchers.

Nieves also spent time with the Arizona Diamondbacks in 2012, making an immediate impact with a two-run home run in his debut. He then signed with the Philadelphia Phillies in 2013, serving as Carlos Ruiz’s backup until a leg injury sidelined him in 2014. A return to the San Diego Padres in 2015 saw him briefly make their opening day roster before being designated for assignment. He finished his playing career with a short stint in the Braves organization in 2015.

Following his playing days, Nieves transitioned into coaching. In 2019, he joined the Boston Red Sox organization as a coach for their Class A-Advanced affiliate, the Salem Red Sox, bringing his extensive baseball experience to player development. Throughout his career, Nieves was known as a solid defensive catcher and a respected teammate.

title: Félix María Zuloaga
text:
Félix María Zuloaga Trillo (1803-1898) was a Mexican conservative general and politician central to the outbreak of the Reform War in 1858, and briefly served as president of Mexico. His early career involved military service, beginning with a colonelcy in 1834 and campaigns against indigenous groups. He defended the government during the Federalist Revolt of 1840 and participated in revisions to the constitution. During the Mexican-American War, he focused on fortifications, and later served as an alderman in Chihuahua before returning to the military. He initially aligned with the liberal forces under Ignacio Comonfort, even commanding troops for him, but this allegiance shifted dramatically.

The pivotal moment came in 1857 with the drafting of a new constitution, sparking conservative opposition due to its reforms targeting the Church and communal land ownership through the Ley Lerdo. As tensions escalated, Zuloaga, initially loyal to Comonfort, became a key conspirator in the Plan of Tacubaya, which sought to overturn the constitution and establish a new congress. This plan led to the overthrow of Comonfort, with Zuloaga assuming the presidency in January 1858 after Comonfort released Benito Juárez, the rightful constitutional president, and fled the country.

Zuloaga's presidency was marked by immediate conflict with Juárez's liberal government. While Zuloaga’s forces experienced initial military successes, capturing key cities and briefly even imprisoning Juárez, the liberals maintained control over peripheral regions, particularly the strategic port of Veracruz. Despite these victories, Zuloaga faced internal divisions within the conservative ranks – Santanistas, Zuloaguistas, and Fusionists – and struggled with financial difficulties. Attempts to revive a centralized government and suppress dissent further complicated his position.

The tide turned against Zuloaga in December 1858 when a moderate conservative faction, the Fusionists, launched a counter-pronouncement. Unable to quell the rebellion, and facing dwindling support, Zuloaga resigned and sought asylum in the British legation.  Manuel Robles Pezuela then assumed the presidency, attempting a compromise with the liberals.  However, this effort failed, and Miguel Miramon was later elected president with Zuloaga's endorsement, effectively relinquishing his claim to the office.

Zuloaga briefly re-emerged after the war, attempting to reclaim the presidency while conservative guerillas remained active, but this proved unsuccessful. He subsequently left Mexico, returning during the Second Mexican Empire but playing no significant political or military role. Following the Empire's collapse in 1867, he was exiled to Cuba before eventually returning to Mexico, where he lived until his death in 1898.

title: Joe McGinniss
text:
Joe McGinniss, born in Manhattan in 1942 and passing away in 2014, was an American author known for his work in both non-fiction and novels, totaling twelve books. He first gained recognition with *The Selling of the President 1968*, a bestseller detailing the marketing strategies used in Richard Nixon’s 1968 presidential campaign. This book, published when he was 26, achieved significant success and established him as a notable figure in political reporting. He later became particularly known for a trilogy of true crime books – *Fatal Vision*, *Blind Faith*, and *Cruel Doubt* – all of which were adapted into television miniseries. His final published work was *The Rogue: Searching for the Real Sarah Palin*, a biography of the former Alaskan governor and 2008 Republican vice-presidential nominee.

McGinniss’s early life was spent in Forest Hills, Queens, and Rye, New York. He attended Archbishop Stepinac High School and later the College of the Holy Cross, graduating in 1964. Despite being proud of his rejection from the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism, he began his journalism career as a general assignment reporter for the *Worcester Telegram* before moving to the *Philadelphia Bulletin* as a sportswriter and then the *Philadelphia Inquirer* as a columnist. He later held a writer-in-residence position at the Los Angeles Herald Examiner and taught creative writing at Bennington College, where he had Donna Tartt and Bret Easton Ellis as students.

Following the success of *The Selling of the President 1968*, McGinniss dedicated himself to writing books full-time. He followed his initial success with a novel, *The Dream Team*, and then *Heroes* and *Going to Extremes*, the latter being a nonfiction account of his experiences in Alaska. The 1980s and early 90s saw him achieve further acclaim with his true crime trilogy. *Fatal Vision* centered on the Jeffrey MacDonald murder case, sparking a lawsuit from MacDonald alleging deception on McGinniss's part regarding his belief in MacDonald's innocence, which ultimately resulted in an out-of-court settlement. The case also became the subject of a book by Janet Malcolm, *The Journalist and the Murderer*, prompting a response from McGinniss himself. *Blind Faith* detailed the Marshall murder case, and *Cruel Doubt* focused on the Lieth Von Stein murder. 

However, his 1993 biography of Ted Kennedy, *The Last Brother*, was widely criticized for its sourcing, lack of attribution, and speculative nature, being described as “awful” and “rotten” by critics. He later returned to Alaska to research Sarah Palin, resulting in *The Rogue*, which generated controversy due to allegations and unnamed sources, and faced potential legal action, though a lawsuit never materialized.  He also briefly pursued a book about the O.J. Simpson trial, ultimately returning a $1 million advance after deciding he couldn't produce a satisfactory work. Later books included *The Miracle of Castel di Sangro* and *Never Enough*. 

In his later years, McGinniss battled alcoholism and depression. He was diagnosed with terminal prostate cancer in 2012 and died in 2014 at the age of 71, leaving behind a legacy as a distinctive and often controversial figure in American journalism and non-fiction writing.

title: John Craven
text:
John Craven, born on August 16th, 1940, is a British journalist and television presenter who is widely recognised for his work on programmes such as Newsround, Countryfile, and Beat the Brain. He was born in Leeds, West Riding of Yorkshire, and received his education at Leeds Modern School. His early life was impacted by his father’s experience as a prisoner of war in Japan during World War II, where he was held for three years.

Craven began his career after leaving school at the age of 16, initially undertaking an apprenticeship at Yorkshire Copperworks and contributing to their company magazine. He then transitioned into print journalism, starting as a junior reporter for the Harrogate Advertiser, followed by work with the Yorkshire Post and freelance writing for various national newspapers. 

He joined the BBC in Newcastle upon Tyne, working in both radio and television, before relocating to the BBC in Bristol in 1970. His most prominent role began in 1972 when he became the original presenter of *John Craven's Newsround*, a children’s news programme which was the first of its kind in British television. The programme utilized the extensive journalistic resources of the BBC and gained recognition for breaking news stories, one notable example being the coverage of the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster in 1986, which occurred just before the programme was due to air. 

Craven's association with children’s television extended beyond Newsround, including appearances delivering news segments on programmes like *Multi-Coloured Swap Shop* and *Saturday Superstore*. He later returned to Newsround in an editorial capacity. After presenting over 3,000 episodes, he left the programme in 1989 and subsequently became a presenter on *Countryfile*, focusing on countryside news. In 2015, he broadened his presenting experience by hosting the BBC Two game show *Beat the Brain*.

Outside of his regular presenting work, Craven participated in Gareth Malone’s All Star Choir in 2014, contributing to a cover version of “Wake Me Up” to benefit BBC’s Children in Need. The choir’s activities were documented in a two-part series, *Gareth's All Star Choir*, broadcast on BBC One in November 2014.  

Craven is actively involved in several charitable organisations, serving as one of nine presidents of the Young People's Trust for the Environment, vice-president of the Waterways Trust, and a Patron of SPANA. He was appointed President of Radio Horton, a hospital radio station serving Banbury’s Horton General Hospital, in July 2016.

Craven is married with two daughters and currently resides in Oxfordshire. He has expressed a desire to continue working as long as possible, enjoying his career immensely. Throughout his career, he has received several accolades, including election to the Royal Television Society in 1996 and the RTS Baird Medal in 2002. He was awarded an OBE in the 2000 New Year Honours for his contributions to children's and rural broadcasting, and is a Fellow of the Linnean Society of London. Newsround itself received a Special Award at the British Academy Children's Awards in 2011, which Craven collected in recognition of the programme’s impact.

title: Martha Cunz
text:
Martha Cunz, born in St. Gallen, Switzerland in 1876 and passing away in 1961, was a Swiss artist primarily recognized for her work as a printmaker. She achieved prominence as one of the first European artists of the 20th century to fully embrace and master the modernist woodcut, and her techniques proved influential to other artists working in the field. 

Cunz received the majority of her artistic education at the Women’s Art School in Munich. There, she studied under Christian Landenberger, Ludwig Schmid-Reutte, and Peter Paul Müller. She furthered her studies in Paris in 1900 with Luc-Olivier Merson and Lucien Simon. Upon returning to Munich the following year, a lithography course led by Ernst Neumann ignited her passion for printmaking. She quickly transitioned to woodcuts, and by 1903, she was a founding member of the German Association of Graphics.

For a considerable period before World War I, Cunz maintained a residence in Munich, making annual visits back to Switzerland. During this time, she travelled throughout Europe, with notable periods spent in Holland in 1904 and 1911, and in Italy in 1914. In 1920, she established a studio at her parents’ home in St. Gallen, where she lived and worked for the rest of her life.

Cunz’s artistic output initially focused on lithographs and, more notably, woodcuts, particularly color woodcuts. She pioneered the use of a Japanese multi-block technique for color printing in Europe. Her style is distinguished by the use of subtly graded, contrasting colors layered to create a luminous effect on the print’s surface. Her work began to gain recognition around 1905, with inclusion in the annual Glass Palace Exhibition in Munich. Early woodcuts were also published in the journal *Deutsche Kunst und Dekoration* in April 1905, alongside pieces by artists like Wassily Kandinsky. 

She produced a total of 71 woodcuts, with the last one completed in 1927, and her final lithographs were created in 1931. Following this, Cunz shifted her focus to painting for approximately two decades, concentrating on landscapes and portraits. She influenced the work of artists like Carl Thiemann and also shared her expertise by teaching printmaking, with Rosa Paul among her students. Several sources detail her life and work, including a dissertation by Daniel Studer from the University of Zürich, and exhibition catalogs focusing on her art and the broader context of Jugendstil (Art Nouveau) printmaking.

title: Andriy Yarmolenko
text:
Andriy Yarmolenko, born in Leningrad in 1989 to Ukrainian parents, is a professional footballer who currently plays as a winger or forward for Dynamo Kyiv and captains the Ukraine national team. His family relocated to Chernihiv, Ukraine, when he was young, and he began playing football at the age of four or five, initially with a self-made ball due to financial constraints. He was first formally coached by Mykola Lypoviy at the Yunist Chernihiv football school.

Yarmolenko's club career began with various Ukrainian clubs including Yunist Chernihiv and Desna Chernihiv before he joined Dynamo Kyiv in 2007. He initially played for Dynamo’s reserve team before debuting for the first team in 2008, scoring the winning goal against Vorskla Poltava. Quickly recognized for his speed and physique, he was dubbed the "new Andriy Shevchenko" by the media. He enjoyed significant success with Dynamo Kyiv, winning the Ukrainian Premier League multiple times (2008-09, 2014-15, 2015-16, 2024-25), the Ukrainian Cup (2013-14, 2014-15), and the Ukrainian Super Cup (2009, 2011, 2016). 

In 2017, Yarmolenko moved to Borussia Dortmund, making his debut as a substitute and later scoring in a Champions League match against Tottenham Hotspur. He then joined West Ham United in 2018, where he experienced both success and injury setbacks. He achieved a memorable brace against Everton, contributing to West Ham’s first Premier League win of the 2018-19 season, but suffered a severe Achilles tendon tear that sidelined him for a significant period. He continued to make contributions upon his return, scoring key goals against Norwich City and Manchester United, and notably scoring the winning goal against Chelsea in 2020. After a period with Al-Ain in the United Arab Emirates, he returned to Dynamo Kyiv in 2023, signing a two-year contract.

Yarmolenko has been a key figure for the Ukraine national team since 2009, earning over 125 caps and scoring 46 goals. He has represented Ukraine in four UEFA European Championships (2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024) and played a vital role in their qualification for Euro 2016. He holds the record for the fastest goal scored by a Ukrainian international player. He recently assisted in Wales qualifying for the 2022 World Cup, though the goal was initially credited to Yarmolenko before being attributed to Gareth Bale.

Beyond football, Yarmolenko is a respected figure in his hometown of Chernihiv, where he was made an honorary citizen in 2021. He has demonstrated considerable philanthropy, donating a substantial sum to the Armed Forces of Ukraine following the Russian invasion in 2022 and actively assisting in the evacuation of his wife’s family. He also presented an ambulance to Chernihiv. In September 2024, he achieved his UEFA "A" coaching license. He has received numerous individual accolades, including being named Ukrainian Footballer of the Year on multiple occasions and winning the Ukrainian Premier League’s Player of the Year award.

title: Salt Bae
text:
Nusret Gökçe, globally known as Salt Bae, was born in 1983 in a village in eastern Turkey to a Kurdish family. His father worked as a mineworker, and financial hardship forced Nusret to leave school at the age of eleven or twelve to begin an apprenticeship as a butcher in Istanbul. Driven to improve his culinary skills, he spent several years between 2007 and 2010 travelling and working in restaurants in Argentina and the United States, often without pay, to gain experience. He opened his first restaurant in Istanbul in 2010, followed by a Dubai location in 2014, laying the foundation for what would become the Nusr-Et chain. The name, meaning “my meat” in Turkish, reflects his focus.

Gökçe rose to international fame in January 2017 through viral videos showcasing his distinctive meat preparation and seasoning technique. His dramatic sprinkling of salt, dropping it from his fingertips down his forearm and onto the meat, earned him the nickname “Salt Bae” and generated millions of views online. This exposure led to patronage from numerous celebrities and political figures.  Nusr-Et now boasts locations in Turkey, Greece, the United States, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia.

Despite his fame, early critical reviews of his New York City steakhouse in 2018 were largely negative, with some describing the food as overpriced, over-salted, tough, and lacking flavor. However, the theatrical aspect of his tableside service, personally performed by Gökçe, was often praised as a unique dining experience. His Manhattan burger bar ultimately closed in 2023.

Gökçe’s career hasn’t been without controversy. He faced criticism for a 2016 photo mimicking Fidel Castro, and for serving Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro amidst widespread food shortages in Venezuela, prompting protests.  He also settled a lawsuit with former employees in New York who accused him of unfairly retaining a portion of their tips, paying them $230,000.  Further issues included a fire at his Istanbul restaurant caused by a show, and temporary closures of his Boston restaurant for violating COVID-19 safety regulations.  A large bill at his UK restaurant also drew media attention.  Most recently, he was investigated by FIFA for disruptive behavior following the 2022 FIFA World Cup final, where he gained unauthorized access to the field and interacted with players and the trophy. Financial reports from his London restaurant show fluctuating revenues and profits, alongside accusations of tip theft and discrimination against former staff. 

Beyond his restaurants, Gökçe has engaged in philanthropic endeavors, funding the construction of a school, library, guest house, mosque, English education center, and computer laboratory in his hometown of Erzurum.

title: Cobhams Asuquo
text:
Cobhams Asuquo, born January 6, 1981, is a Nigerian musician, producer, and songwriter. Beginning his career after working at Questionmark Entertainment, he established his own recording facility and later co-managed CAMP (Cobhams Asuquo Music Productions) alongside Bez Idakula and Stan Iyke. He later founded Vintage Gray Media Ltd., which produced the music countdown show “The Top 12 Countdown with Cobhams Asuquo,” consisting of 74 episodes.

Initially trained as a lawyer, Asuquo gained prominence producing for other artists. He notably produced Asa’s debut album, co-writing hit singles like "Fire on the Mountain" and "Jailer." Throughout the early 2000s and continuing afterward, he produced numerous successful tracks for a wide array of Nigerian artists, including Maintain, Omawumi, Djinne, Banky W, and Tiwa Savage, among many others. 

Beyond studio production, Asuquo has performed internationally with bands at events like the Harare International Festival of Arts and concerts in France, South Africa, and Nigeria. He has also contributed to film and television, composing and arranging scores for projects such as “A Voice for Ella” and “Bayelsan Sillhouttes.”

Asuquo’s involvement extends to global advocacy. He performed at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, and participated in events with Bono’s ONE Campaign, raising awareness for agriculture in Nigeria and contributing to the US-Africa summit. He produced the anthem "Strong Girl" for the ‘Poverty is Sexist’ campaign, later remixing it with Bono, and co-produced "Tell Everyone" for the UN Global Goals campaign, featuring artists from across Africa. He performed at the Global Citizen Festival in New York City to further promote the UN Global Goals. He has also held production roles with Coke Studio Africa and events like Rhythm Unplugged and Hennessy Artistry.

As a recording artist in his own right, Asuquo released his debut single “Ordinary People” in 2014, followed by several others including “Do the Right Thing” featuring Bez, “Star of Wonder,” “Boosit” featuring Falz, “The Other Room,” “Adore,” and most recently, “We Plenti” featuring Simi in 2019. Despite being visually impaired, Asuquo has built a highly successful career. He married Ojuolape Veronica Olukanni in 2010, and they have two sons together.

title: Gopi Sundar
text:
Gopi Sundar C.S., born May 30, 1977, in Kochi, Kerala, is a versatile Indian artist working as a music director, programmer, playback singer, songwriter, actor, and performer across the Malayalam, Telugu, and Tamil film industries. He began his musical journey composing jingles, creating nearly 5,000 of them over several years, aided by guidance from Sudheer Kariat. He also gained experience as a keyboardist, collaborating with prominent Bollywood composers Vishal–Shekhar on songs like “Ek Main Aur Ek Tu Hai” and “Aankhon mein teri.”

Sundar’s formal musical education was brief, having dropped out of Government Music College in Chennai after feeling disillusioned. He found early support from his father, who connected him with Malayalam composer Ouseppachan, becoming his assistant for over a decade. His breakthrough came with the film *Notebook* in 2005, leading to his first independent film score. He quickly followed this with *Flash*, his first complete soundtrack composition. A pivotal moment in his career was *Big B*, a film that debuted several technicians and showcased Sundar's ability to create a fresh cinematic experience with his music. 

He expanded his work to Tamil cinema with *Poi Solla Porom* in 2008, and experienced success with *Sagar Alias Jackie Reloaded*, despite critical reception of the film itself. The film *Anwar* (2010) earned him his first Filmfare Award for Best Music Director. *Ustad Hotel* (2012) proved to be a major success, with the song “Appangalembadum” becoming a chart-topping hit and garnering him multiple awards, including Filmfare, Asianet, SIIMA, and Kochi Times Awards.

Sundar’s contributions extended to Bollywood with the song “Titli” for *Chennai Express* (2013). He continued to deliver successful soundtracks for films like *1983*, which won him the National Film Award for Best Background Score, and *Bangalore Days*, earning him further Filmfare and Asianet awards. He ventured into acting with a cameo in *Salalah Mobiles*. He further expanded his presence into the Telugu film industry with *Malli Malli Idi Rani Roju* and *Bhale Bhale Magadivoy*. 

In recent years, his work on *Pulimurugan* garnered international attention, being considered for Academy Award nominations for both Best Original Song and Best Original Score. He continues to be a prolific composer, with credits including *Oopiri*, *Devi*, and *Geetha Govindam*. Sundar launched his own recording label, Gopi Sundar Music Company, to support emerging musicians, and formed the live performance band “Band Big G” in Dubai. He frequently collaborates with directors like Rosshan Andrrews and Amal Neerad, and lyricists Rafeeq Ahamed, Santhosh Varma and B.K Harinarayanan.

title: Yuu Watase
text:
Yuu Watase was born on March 5, 1970, in Kishiwada, Osaka, and began her career as a manga artist at the young age of 18 in 1989 with a short story titled “Pajama de Ojama.” Since then, she has created a substantial body of work, publishing over 50 volumes encompassing both one-shot stories and long-running manga series. She is particularly well-known for her popular series *Fushigi Yûgi*. 

Watase initially pursued formal art training after high school, attending a private art school focused on manga. However, she left the school mid-course, as she had already debuted her first work. She has a preference for traditional art methods, believing they allow for more emotional expression in her work, although she has experimented with digital programs like Adobe Photoshop to enhance her traditional artwork.

Throughout her career, Watase has faced challenges. She recounted an experience with an editor during the serialization of *Arata: The Legend*, where she was repeatedly asked to redraw scenes, leading to exhausting workdays and a diminishing passion for the project. The constant need for approval overshadowed her creative drive and connection to the story and its fans. 

In 2019, Watase publicly came out as X-gender, a Japanese non-binary gender identity. Viz Media, which publishes some of her work in English, clarified that her preferred pronouns remain "she" and "her" in English translations. 

Watase’s extensive catalog includes series published under various imprints. Her major works published under Flower Comics include the *Fushigi Yûgi* series (including multiple spin-offs like *Genbu Kaiden* and the ongoing *Byakko Senki*), *Ceres, Celestial Legend*, *Alice 19th*, and *Absolute Boyfriend*. She also ventured into the shōnen genre with *Arata: The Legend*, published by Shōnen Sunday Comics. Beyond her serialized works, she has numerous short stories and collections published under titles like *YuuTopia Collection* and *Yuu Watase Best Selection*.  Furthermore, many of her series have been re-released in different formats, including *bunko* editions and *kanzenban* editions, and she has also created numerous artbooks and illustrated novels related to her manga.

In 1998, Watase received the 43rd Shogakukan Manga Award in the shōjo category for *Ceres, Celestial Legend*, acknowledging her significant contributions to the manga industry.

title: Isla Fisher
text:
Isla Lang Fisher, born in Oman in 1976 to Scottish parents, is an Australian actress who began her career in commercials before gaining recognition for her role as Shannon Reed on the Australian soap opera *Home and Away* from 1994 to 1997. During her time on the show, she received two Logie Award nominations. She transitioned to Hollywood in 2002 with a part in *Scooby-Doo*, and has since appeared in numerous films including *Wedding Crashers* (2005), *Confessions of a Shopaholic* (2009), *The Great Gatsby* (2013) and *Now You See Me* (2013). She has also lent her voice to animated features like *Horton Hears a Who!* (2008) and *Rango* (2011). 

Fisher’s early life was spent moving from Oman to Scotland and then to Perth, Australia, when she was six. She describes herself as feeling very Australian and having a laid-back attitude to life. She attended Swanbourne Primary School and Methodist Ladies’ College and actively participated in school theatre productions.  At 21, she pursued further training at L'École Internationale de Théâtre Jacques Lecoq in Paris, studying clowning, mime, and musical theatre. Prior to her success as an actress, she even published two young adult novels.

After leaving *Home and Away*, Fisher continued to hone her skills with theatre work in the UK and a role in a German slasher film before finding success in Hollywood. *Wedding Crashers* proved to be a breakthrough role, earning her a Best Breakthrough Performance Award at the MTV Movie Awards. She continued to take on diverse roles, including parts in the thriller *The Lookout* and the comedy *Hot Rod*.  She also voiced characters in animated films, winning an Alliance of Women Film Journalists Award for her work in *Rango*. 

Fisher starred in *The Great Gatsby* and *Now You See Me* in 2013, cementing her mainstream recognition. She also took on a recurring role in the Netflix revival of *Arrested Development* and has starred in the comedy-drama series *Wolf Like Me* since 2022. Beyond acting, she has continued to write, authoring both young adult novels and the *Marge in Charge* book series. 

From 2010 until 2025, Fisher was married to English comedian Sacha Baron Cohen, and they have three children together. Throughout her career, she has described herself as fortunate, acknowledging the sometimes unpredictable nature of the industry, and expressed gratitude for the opportunities she’s been given.

title: Karl Eliasberg
text:
Karl Eliasberg was a Soviet conductor born in Minsk in 1907 and passing away in Leningrad in 1978. He initially trained as a violinist, graduating from the Leningrad Conservatory in 1929, and began his conducting career with the Leningrad Theatre of Musical Comedy before moving to Leningrad Radio. Though he was only the second conductor of the Leningrad Philharmonic, Eliasberg became a pivotal figure during the siege of Leningrad in World War II.

He is most renowned for conducting the premiere of Dmitri Shostakovich’s Seventh Symphony, dedicated to the city during the siege, on August 9th, 1942. This performance was particularly remarkable because only fifteen musicians were available, many having perished from starvation or joined the military. Eliasberg worked tirelessly to gather musicians from various orchestras and military bands, and also ensured they received food during the desperate circumstances, effectively saving lives. The broadcast performance significantly boosted the morale of the city’s surviving population.

Despite this heroic act and being awarded the title of Meritorious Artist of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic in 1944, Eliasberg’s career in Leningrad was hampered by the return of Yevgeny Mravinsky, who effectively sidelined him. He spent much of his post-war career as a travelling, provincial conductor, only appearing in Leningrad three more times. These appearances were all connected to performances of Shostakovich’s Seventh Symphony, using the reserve orchestra. 

A particularly poignant reunion occurred in 1964, when Eliasberg conducted the first movement of the symphony with 22 of the original musicians, in the presence of Shostakovich himself, twenty-two years after their historic performance. He dedicated that concert to those who had participated in the 1942 performance but had since died. He later reflected on the experience, acknowledging both the joy and the sorrow of remembering the past.

Eliasberg’s contributions were largely forgotten after his death in 1978, and he was initially buried in an unremarkable grave. However, after the fall of Communism, his legacy was revived by Yuri Temirkanov, and his remains were moved to a more prominent location at the Volkovo Cemetery. He left behind a number of recordings including works by Brahms, Mahler, Shostakovich, Taneyev, and Bach. His 1942 performance of Shostakovich’s Seventh Symphony has been the subject of a novel and featured in both films and radio documentaries.

title: Raghav Juyal
text:
Raghav Juyal, born on July 10, 1991, is a multi-talented Indian performer working as an actor, dancer, choreographer, and television presenter. He initially gained widespread recognition as a contestant on the dance reality show *Dance India Dance 3* in 2012. Despite not being initially selected for the Top 18, public demand and the intervention of judge Mithun Chakraborty brought him back as a “trump card,” ultimately leading him to the second runner-up position with a significant number of votes. He became known for his unique dance style and popularized the “Slow Motion Walk” in India, a move that distinguished him from other dancers.

Following his success on *Dance India Dance*, Juyal became a skipper on *DID Li’l Masters 2*, successfully guiding both of his students to the Grand Finale. He continued in a leadership role, captaining a team to victory on *Dance Ke Superkids*.  He transitioned into acting with a role in the 2014 comedy *Sonali Cable*, where critics praised his vibrant performance and screen presence, with some stating he outshone the leads. He then appeared in the dance film *ABCD 2* in 2015.

Juyal has become a prominent television host, presenting several seasons of the dance reality show *Dance Plus* on Star Plus. He also hosted or co-hosted other shows including *Prem Ki Diwali*, *Khatron Ke Khiladi 7*, *Star Parivaar Awards*, *Colors Golden Petal Awards*, *Timeless Aisha*, *Rising Star*, *Dance Champions*, *Dil Hai Hindustani*, and *Dance Plus* seasons 4 and 5. 

His film career continued with roles in *Nawabzaade* (2018), *Street Dancer 3D* (2020), and *Bahut Hua Samman* (2020), the latter of which garnered positive reviews.  He also ventured into darker roles, appearing in the second season of the web series *Abhay* as a negative character.  He starred in the romantic movie *Wedlock* which was scheduled for release in August 2021 and was also part of the cast of *Yudhra*, a film produced by Excel Entertainment, slated for release in 2022. Most recently, in 2024, he starred in the action thriller *Kill* and won an IIFA Award in 2025 for Best Performance in a Negative Role.

Raghav Juyal was born and raised in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, to parents Deepak Juyal, a lawyer, and Alka Bakshi Juyal. He is of Garhwali Brahmin descent and attended Doon International School and DAV (PG) College. He is self-taught in dance, learning through observation of performances online and on television, and was mentored in acting by Saurabh Sachdeva.

title: Zubaira Tukhugov
text:
Zubaira Tukhugov, born January 15, 1991, is a Russian mixed martial artist who competed in the Lightweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). He began his professional MMA career in 2010, initially gaining experience by winning a Pankration Atrium Cup eight-man tournament. Before joining the UFC in 2014, Tukhugov built a record of 10-3, fighting for promotions including Cage Warriors, ProFC, and Fight Nights, where he won three consecutive bouts against Romano De Los Reyes, Harun Kina, and Vaso Bakocevic. He also secured a victory over Denys Pidnebesnyi while competing in Cage Warriors.

Tukhugov debuted in the UFC in February 2014 with a unanimous decision win over Douglas Silva de Andrade, after his original opponent, Thiago Tavares, withdrew due to injury. He followed this with a first-round technical knockout victory over Ernest Chavez in October of the same year. A scheduled rematch with Tavares in 2015 was cancelled due to a rib injury sustained by Tukhugov. He later won a split decision against Phillipe Nover in December 2015.

His UFC career has been marked by both successes and setbacks. A controversial split decision loss to Renato Moicano in May 2016 followed two disputed decisions regarding strikes to the groin. In 2016, he was pulled from a fight after a potential anti-doping violation, eventually resulting in a two-year USADA suspension and a $10,000 fine for testing positive for ostarine. He was also removed from a scheduled fight in 2018 due to his involvement in the post-fight melee at UFC 229 following the Khabib Nurmagomedov vs. Conor McGregor event, receiving a one-year suspension and a $25,000 fine, later reduced by 35 days.  

Following his suspension, Tukhugov returned in 2019, fighting to a split draw against Lerone Murphy. He secured another first-round TKO victory over Kevin Aguilar in 2020, but lost a split decision to Hakeem Dawodu at UFC 253, having missed the featherweight limit. Further fights saw a unanimous decision win over Ricardo Ramos in 2021, and scheduled bouts against Nate Landwehr and Lucas Almeida both fall through due to visa issues and weight management problems, respectively. His final UFC fight in February 2023, against Elves Brenner, ended in a split decision loss after he again missed weight. Subsequently, on February 28, 2023, he was released from the UFC roster.

title: Bobby Thomson
text:
Bobby Thomson, born in Glasgow, Scotland in 1923 and passing away in 2010, was a Major League Baseball outfielder known for a career spanning several teams including the New York Giants, Milwaukee Braves, Chicago Cubs, Boston Red Sox, and Baltimore Orioles. Though he achieved eight seasons with 20 or more home runs and was a three-time All-Star, he is overwhelmingly remembered for one singular moment: the “Shot Heard ‘Round the World.”

Thomson’s family moved to Staten Island, New York when he was two years old, and he signed with the Giants directly out of high school in 1942. His baseball career was interrupted by World War II, serving in the United States Army Air Forces as a bombardier, though he remained stateside. He began his professional baseball career in earnest in 1947, posting a .283 batting average with 29 home runs in his rookie season. He continued to be a productive hitter, achieving a career-best .309 average and 109 RBIs in 1949.

The 1951 season cemented Thomson’s place in baseball lore. Despite being 13 1/2 games behind the Brooklyn Dodgers in mid-August, the Giants rallied to tie for the National League pennant, forcing a three-game playoff. The deciding game, played at the Polo Grounds, saw the Dodgers leading 4-1 in the bottom of the ninth. After a series of hits, Thomson came to bat with the score 4-2 and runners on second and third. His dramatic walk-off home run off pitcher Ralph Branca won the pennant for the Giants and became instantly legendary, broadcast coast-to-coast as the first major sporting event to receive such coverage. However, the Giants lost the subsequent World Series to the New York Yankees, four games to two, with Thomson batting .238.

Later revelations brought controversy to the celebrated moment. It was discovered in 2001, and detailed in a 2008 book, that the Giants had been systematically stealing signs from opposing catchers using a telescope and a buzzer system. Though Thomson maintained he was unaware of the stolen signs, evidence suggested that information regarding the pitch was relayed to him before his famous at-bat. 

Thomson continued playing for several years, leading the National League in triples in 1952 and being traded back to the Giants in 1957. He finished his major league career in 1960 and played one final season in Japan in 1963. Throughout his 15-year career, he compiled a .270 batting average, 264 home runs, and 1,026 RBIs. Following his playing days, he worked in sales. He was honored with the naming of baseball fields in Scotland and Staten Island after him, and is a member of the Staten Island Sports Hall of Fame. A poignant letter received decades later from a Marine serving in Korea, whose dying friend had listened to the broadcast of Thomson’s home run, highlighted the profound impact of that moment beyond the confines of the baseball field.

title: Shaolin (humorist)
text:
Francisco Jozenilton Veloso, professionally known as Shaolin, was a Brazilian entertainer who worked as a cartoonist, caricaturist, humorist, comedian and television presenter. Born on May 8, 1971, in Coremas, Paraíba, he became a recognizable figure in Brazilian media before his death on January 14, 2016.

Shaolin began his career performing at the Teatro Municipal Severino Cabral in Campina Grande. He expanded his work into radio, hosting programs on Rádio Campina Grande, and further developed his artistic skills by creating cartoons for several publications, including the newspapers *A Palavra* and *Jornal da Paraíba*, as well as *Revista Nordeste*. 

He gained widespread recognition for his appearances on popular Brazilian television programs. He featured in shows like *Domingão do Faustão* and *Show do Tom*, but he is perhaps best remembered for his work on *Tudo è Possível*, hosted by Ana Hickmann. On this show, Shaolin specialized in satirical impressions of Brazilian celebrities. His targets included well-known figures such as the singer Leonardo, Joelma, of the band Banda Calypso, and Zezé di Camargo. 

In January 2011, Shaolin suffered life-altering injuries in a serious traffic accident. His car collided with a truck on the BR-230 highway near Campina Grande. The accident left him in a coma for several months, until May of that year, when he was discharged from the hospital. However, he did not fully recover from his injuries and continued to require care. Despite his severe condition, Shaolin showed remarkable resilience. By September 2012, he was able to begin communicating through deliberate movements of his eyelid, aided by a specialized machine.

Shaolin was married to Laudiceia Veloso in December 1994, and together they had two children. His death, occurring on January 14, 2016, was the result of a myocardial infarction, marking the end of a career that brought humor to many Brazilians. Information about his life and career can be found on the Internet Movie Database (IMDb) and through his previously active Twitter account.

title: Charmion King
text:
Charmion King, a Canadian actress, was born in Toronto, Ontario on July 25, 1925, and passed away there on January 6, 2007, at the age of 81. Her career blossomed during the growth of Canada’s theatre and television scene in the 1950s. She began her acting journey immediately after completing her studies at Hart House at the University of Toronto. 

King quickly gained recognition for her appearance and talent, securing roles at the Crest Theatre and participating in the Straw Hat Players’ summer performances in the Muskoka Lake region. This early work served as a springboard for larger opportunities, leading to her involvement with the prestigious Stratford Festival. During her time at Stratford, she performed in several significant productions, including *The Winter’s Tale*, *Three Sisters*, and *Uncle Vanya*.  

Her career extended beyond Canada, as she made an appearance on Broadway, performing in Tyrone Guthrie’s production of *Love and Libel*. King also became a familiar face on television, landing roles in several well-known productions. She portrayed Josephine Barry in the classic television film *Anne of Green Gables* and took on the role of Rose Fitzgerald Kennedy in *Jackie, Ethel, Joan: The Women of Camelot*. 

Furthermore, she starred in two Canadian television series, *Wind at My Back* and *House of Pride*, demonstrating her consistent presence in the Canadian entertainment industry.  In 1988, she also appeared in the film *Shadow Dancing*.

Beyond her individual accomplishments, Charmion King’s life was deeply intertwined with that of another prominent Canadian actor, Gordon Pinsent, whom she married. Their marriage lasted for 44 years. Their family connection to the arts continued with their daughter, Leah Pinsent, who also became a recognized actress in Canadian television. According to reports, King’s death was due to complications stemming from emphysema.

title: Bobby Fischer
text:
Robert James Fischer, born in Chicago in 1943, was an American chess grandmaster who became the eleventh World Chess Champion. A child prodigy, he displayed exceptional chess ability from a young age, winning his first of a record eight US Championships at just 14 years old. In 1964, he achieved a historic perfect score of 11-0 in the US Championship, a feat unmatched in the tournament’s history. His path to the World Championship involved dominating qualifying matches, including sweeping victories against Mark Taimanov and Bent Larsen with 6-0 scores, and defeating Tigran Petrosian.

The 1972 World Championship match against Boris Spassky in Reykjavík, Iceland, was a globally publicized event, framed as a Cold War contest between the United States and the Soviet Union. Fischer’s victory in this match garnered unprecedented worldwide attention for chess. However, in 1975, Fischer refused to defend his title due to disagreements with FIDE, the international chess governing body, over match conditions. As a result, Anatoly Karpov was declared the World Champion by default.

Following this, Fischer largely withdrew from public life, with occasional reports surfacing regarding his increasingly erratic behavior. He reemerged in 1992 to play an unofficial rematch against Spassky in Yugoslavia, which was then under a United Nations embargo. This decision brought him into conflict with the US government, which warned him against violating sanctions. A warrant was issued for his arrest, leading him to live as an exile. In 2004, he was arrested in Japan for traveling on a revoked US passport and eventually granted Icelandic citizenship through a special act of the Althing, where he resided until his death in 2008. Throughout his life, Fischer was known for making numerous antisemitic statements, including Holocaust denial, despite his Jewish heritage, and his views and behavior fueled speculation about his psychological state.

Fischer left a lasting legacy on the game of chess. His book, *My 60 Memorable Games*, published in 1969, remains a cornerstone of chess literature. He also innovated chess timing systems, patenting a method of adding time increments after each move – a now-standard practice in tournaments. Furthermore, he invented Fischer Random Chess (Chess960), a variant where the starting position of the pieces is randomized, offering a new dimension to the game.

Fischer’s early life was marked by instability. His mother, Regina Wender Fischer, a physician, raised him and his sister as a single parent after separating from Hans-Gerhardt Fischer. It was later revealed, through investigative reporting, that Paul Neményi, a Hungarian mathematician, was Fischer’s biological father. He learned to play chess at the age of six and quickly became engrossed in the game, eventually finding guidance from Brooklyn Chess Club President Carmine Nigro. He then studied with John Collins at the Hawthorne Chess Club, playing countless games and absorbing knowledge from Collins’ extensive chess library. 

His rise through the chess world was rapid. He won the US Junior Championship in 1956 and the US Open Championship in 1957, becoming the youngest ever to achieve both titles. In 1957/58, at just under 15 years old, he won the US Championship, qualifying him for the 1958 Interzonal tournament, and earning him the title of International Master. He became a Grandmaster, the youngest at the time, showcasing remarkable talent and dedication to the game.

title: Rosé (singer)
text:
Rosé, born Roseanne Park on February 11, 1997, is a New Zealand and South Korean singer and songwriter. She was born in Auckland, New Zealand, and spent her childhood in Melbourne, Australia before moving to Seoul, South Korea in 2012. After successfully auditioning for YG Entertainment in Sydney, she trained for four years and ultimately debuted as a member of the girl group Blackpink in August 2016. 

Before her official debut, Rosé was featured on a song by labelmate G-Dragon in 2012, though her contribution wasn’t publicly credited at the time. As a member of Blackpink, she achieved significant success, including a global partnership with Interscope Records in 2018. Rosé also appeared on Korean broadcast programs, showcasing her vocal ability and gaining positive reception from audiences. 

In March 2021, Rosé embarked on her solo career with the release of her debut single album, *R*. This album broke records, achieving the highest first-week sales for a Korean female soloist, selling 448,089 copies. The lead single, “On the Ground,” further cemented her success, topping the Billboard Global 200 chart – a first for a Korean soloist, as well as a group member - and charting in the UK Singles Chart. She gained six Guinness World Records for this success. 

Following Blackpink's activities, Rosé signed with The Black Label and Atlantic Records in 2024. This led to the release of “Apt.” featuring Bruno Mars, which became another number-one hit on the Billboard Global 200 and topped charts in multiple countries, including Australia, marking the first time a Korean female soloist achieved this in Australia. “Apt.” also reached the top three on both the US Billboard Hot 100 and the UK Singles Chart, breaking records for Korean female soloists on both charts. Her debut studio album *Rosie*, released in December 2024, continued this success, charting highly in the US and the UK.

Throughout her career, Rosé has received awards including two MAMA Awards and the Asia Artist Award for Song of the Year. She is highly influential on social media, ranking as the second-most followed Korean individual on Instagram, and has been featured on both *Time’s* list of the 100 most influential people and *Rolling Stone’s* list of living icons from Australia and New Zealand. 

Beyond music, Rosé has established herself as a fashion icon, serving as a global ambassador for Yves Saint Laurent and Tiffany & Co., and appearing on numerous magazine covers. Her voice has been widely praised for its unique timbre, earning her the nickname "the golden voice" among fans. She has cited artists like Taeyang and Tori Kelly as musical inspirations.

title: Neil Sinclair
text:
Neil Sinclair, born February 23, 1974, was a professional boxer from Northern Ireland who competed between 1995 and 2010. His career encompassed both significant amateur achievements and a decade and a half in the professional ranks, culminating in a challenge for a world title. 

Sinclair began his boxing journey as an amateur, representing Ireland with success. In 1992, he earned a bronze medal at the Junior World Championships held in Montreal. He continued to demonstrate his talent, notably winning a gold medal representing Northern Ireland at the 1994 Commonwealth Games in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. These early accomplishments laid the foundation for his professional career.

Sinclair transitioned to professional boxing in April 1995, making his debut at the Ulster Hall in Belfast. He secured a knockout victory over Marty Duke in his first fight, appearing on a card that also featured Darren Corbett and marked the final professional bout for Damien Denny. He continued to build his professional record over the following years. 

A period of relative inactivity saw Sinclair announce his retirement in June 2007. However, his passion for the sport led to a swift return to the ring within a couple of months. He continued to fight, and in May 2009, achieved a victory on home soil at the Odyssey Arena in Belfast, winning the Irish light-middleweight title with a stoppage against Henry Coyle.

Throughout his professional career, Sinclair also held the British welterweight title from 2001 to 2003, establishing himself as a prominent fighter at the national level. He also challenged for the EBU European Union title once in 2008. The peak of his professional career came in 2010 when he received the opportunity to compete for the WBO welterweight title, though the article does not specify the outcome of this fight. 

Details of his complete professional boxing record can be found on BoxRec, although registration is required to access it. Further information regarding his participation in the Commonwealth Games is archived on the Commonwealth Games Federation website.

title: Joel Edgerton
text:
Joel Edgerton, born in Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia in 1974, is a versatile actor and filmmaker with a substantial body of work spanning Australian and international productions. He began his career on the stage and in Australian television, gaining recognition for his role as Will McGill in the series *The Secret Life of Us*, for which he received an AACTA Award. He initially gained wider international attention playing Owen Lars in *Star Wars: Attack of the Clones* and *Revenge of the Sith*, a role he revisited in the Disney+ series *Obi-Wan Kenobi*.

Throughout his career, Edgerton has consistently appeared in a diverse range of films. Notable Australian contributions include *The Square*, *Animal Kingdom*—winning him another AACTA Award—*Wish You Were Here*, and *Felony*. He’s also featured in major international films like *King Arthur*, *Warrior*, *Zero Dark Thirty*, *The Great Gatsby*, *Black Mass*, *Bright*, *The Green Knight*, *Master Gardener*, and *The Boys in the Boat*. Beyond film, he’s appeared in television series such as *The Underground Railroad* and the science fiction series *Dark Matter*.

Edgerton’s talents extend beyond acting; he is a skilled filmmaker. He wrote, directed, and starred in the critically acclaimed thriller *The Gift* (2015), earning him a nomination for a DGA Award. He followed this success with *Boy Erased* (2018), which he also wrote and directed, and co-wrote *The King* the following year. He’s also lent his voice to animated projects, including *Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole* and a guest appearance voicing a character in the children’s show *Bluey*. 

His personal life includes a past relationship with Olympic athlete Cathy Freeman and a current relationship with Christine Centenera, editor-in-chief of Vogue Australia, with whom he has twins born in 2021. He comes from a creative family, with his brother Nash Edgerton working as a stuntman and filmmaker; the two have collaborated on several projects, including the film *Gringo*, and are both part of the Blue-Tongue Films collective. 

Edgerton is also committed to philanthropic work, serving as a distinguished ambassador for The Fred Hollows Foundation, an organization dedicated to restoring sight and improving eye health globally and within Australia. He views this work as a meaningful counterbalance to the demands of his profession. He received the Australians in Film Breakthrough Award in 2011, recognizing his accomplishments in international cinema.

title: Tappaya Sit-Or
text:
Tappaya Sit Or, also known as Mit Klinmee, born February 1, 1976, is a retired Muay Thai fighter who achieved championship status at Rajadamnern and the World Muay Thai Council (WMC). He reached the number one ranking at Lumpini Stadium, though he didn’t secure the championship title there. Following his fighting career, he transitioned into coaching and currently owns and operates Sor Klinmee Gym in Pattaya, Thailand.

Tappaya comes from a large family, being the youngest of eleven children. He began training and fighting at a very young age, starting at six years old alongside his brother, Yokthai Sit-Or, and nephew, Rambaa Somdet. Their early training consisted of rigorous sessions before and after school, followed by regular fights in local bars for financial gain. By the age of twelve, Tappaya was already competing in Bangkok. The three fighters were foundational to the original Sit Or camp in Pattaya, moving there from Petrungruang gym; the camp later relocated to Bangkok and became known for producing notable fighters like Nong-O Sit-Or and Petchmankong Petfergus.

The peak of Tappaya’s career came in 1997. He won the 61.5 kg Rajadamnern belt by defeating Ankandet BaoBaoin, a fight televised nationally on Channel 5. He held this title for three consecutive years. In the same year, on August 10th, he secured the WMC belt at 61.5 kg with a victory over Panmongkon Carryboy. He gained significant exposure during this period, becoming a prominent fighter on Channel 7. Throughout his career, which concluded in 2001, Tappaya amassed an impressive record of 200 wins, 36 losses, and 5 draws. 

Beyond Thailand, Tappaya broadened his martial arts experience towards the end of his fighting career by traveling to China, Japan, and the United Kingdom to both teach and compete. While in Japan, he participated in both kickboxing and mixed martial arts, notably defeating Hayato in a kickboxing match while representing Crosspoint Gym. 

After retiring, Tappaya realized a long-held ambition and opened Sor Klinmee Gym in 2009, located on Neung Phap Wan road in Pattaya. He serves as the gym's owner and head trainer. Currently, he guides several fighters who are actively competing in the major stadiums of Bangkok, including Robert Sor Klinmee, a southpaw fighting at 46 kg in Rajadamnern Stadium, and Sangpet Sor Klinmee, an orthodox fighter competing at 45.5 kg in both Rajadamnern and Lumpini. Other notable trainees include Sinsamut Klinmee, his brother Sudsakorn Sor Klinmee, and the son of Yokthai, Thepprasit champion Fasai Sor Klinmee, alongside several younger, developing boxers.

title: Bhāskara I
text:
Bhāskara I was a 7th-century Indian mathematician and astronomer, considered a pivotal figure in the continuation of Aryabhata’s astronomical school. Born in India around 600 AD, and likely an astronomer by profession, he received his education from his father. While details of his life are sparse, references in his writings suggest he may have been born in Saurastra, in present-day Gujarat, and later moved to Aśmaka. He is recognized alongside Brahmagupta as one of the most important Indian mathematicians of his time, both contributing significantly to the study of fractions.

Bhāskara’s most significant contribution lies in his representation of numbers. While positional numeral systems existed before his time, they were expressed through words and allegories – the number one as the moon, two as wings, five as the senses – arranged in reverse order of powers of ten. Bhāskara was the first to openly use the Brahmi numerals in a scientific text, specifically his commentary on Aryabhata’s work, the *Āryabhaṭīyabhāṣya*, written in 629 AD. This commentary is one of the oldest known prose works in Sanskrit dedicated to mathematics and astronomy. He wrote numbers left to right, in descending values, much like our modern decimal system, and explicitly explained the numeral system using the phrase "ankair api" ("in figures this reads") alongside the Brahmi numerals, including a symbol for zero.

Beyond this crucial development, Bhāskara authored two further astronomical texts: the *Mahābhāskarīya* ("Great Book of Bhāskara") and the *Laghubhāskarīya* ("Small Book of Bhāskara"). The *Mahābhāskarīya* is an eight-chapter work covering mathematical astronomy, including planetary longitudes, conjunctions, eclipses, and planetary movements. He also made substantial contributions to mathematical formulas. Notably, he provided a remarkably accurate rational approximation for the sine function, with a relative error of less than 1.9%, which he attributed to Aryabhata. He explored relationships between sine and cosine, and angles in different quadrants. 

Bhāskara also tackled what are now known as Pell's equations, posing problems like finding a square that, when multiplied by eight and increased by one, results in another square. He demonstrated solutions to these types of equations, such as (1,3) and (6,17). He also clearly stated his belief that pi (π) was an irrational number, criticizing the common Jain practice of approximating it as the square root of ten. He was the first to discuss quadrilaterals with four unequal, non-parallel sides. Parts of his *Mahābhāskarīya* were later translated into Arabic, extending his influence beyond India. 

In recognition of his contributions, the Indian Space Research Organisation named the Bhāskara I satellite, launched in 1979, in his honor.

title: Shawn Ashmore
text:
Shawn Ashmore, born October 7, 1979, in Richmond, British Columbia, is a Canadian actor with a diverse career spanning film, television, and video games. He began acting as a child, landing his first role after his twin brother Aaron was initially cast in a commercial but became ill. The brothers were sometimes chosen for parts by a coin flip early in their careers. Ashmore received a Gemini Award nomination at age 14 for his leading role in the TV film *Guitarman* (1994).

He gained prominence in the late 1990s and early 2000s with roles in television series like *Animorphs* (1998-1999) and *In a Heartbeat* (2000-2001), and the Disney Channel Original Movie *Cadet Kelly* (2002). However, international recognition came with his portrayal of Bobby Drake / Iceman in the *X-Men* film franchise, beginning in 2000 and continuing through 2014. He won an MTV Movie Award for Breakthrough Male Performance for *X2* (2003).

Beyond the *X-Men* films, Ashmore took on leading roles in movies like *Terry* (2005), a biopic about Terry Fox, and horror films *The Ruins* (2008) and *Frozen* (2010). On television, he played FBI agent Mike Weston in *The Following* (2013–2015) and currently stars as attorney Wesley Evers in the police procedural *The Rookie* (2018–present), becoming a series regular in the third season. 

Ashmore has also made significant inroads into the video game industry, providing voice and performance capture for characters in *Quantum Break* (2016), *The Dark Pictures Anthology: Man of Medan* (2019), and *Alan Wake II* (2023). His work in *Quantum Break* was particularly lauded, with critics praising his nuanced performance.

Throughout his career, Ashmore has received a Leo Award for *Legend of Earthsea* (2004) and multiple Gemini and Saturn Award nominations. He often works alongside his identical twin brother, Aaron Ashmore, with whom he shared a scene in the *Fringe* episode “Amber 31422” after fifteen years of not acting together. 

Ashmore married Dana Renee Wasdin in 2012, whom he met on the set of *Frozen*. They have one son, Oliver, born in 2017. Both brothers have matching “GMA” tattoos honoring their step-grandfather, Gangu Jagtiani. He has also used his platform to support breast cancer awareness causes, participating in fundraising events.

title: Mike Adenuga
text:
Michael Adenuga Jr., born April 29, 1953, is a Nigerian businessman currently ranked as the fifth richest person in Africa, with Forbes estimating his net worth at $6.7 billion as of May 2024. He is primarily known as the owner of Globacom, Nigeria’s second-largest telecommunications company, which also operates in Ghana and Benin. Beyond telecoms, Adenuga holds significant stakes in Equitorial Trust Bank and the oil exploration company, Conoil, originally known as Consolidated Oil Company.

Adenuga’s background reflects a blend of educational and entrepreneurial pursuits. His father was a schoolteacher, and his mother a businesswoman with royal lineage from the Ijebu people of Nigeria. He identifies as Yoruba. He completed his secondary education at Ibadan Grammar School and Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro, and financed his university studies, in part, by working as a taxi driver. He ultimately earned degrees in Business Administration from Northwestern Oklahoma State University and Pace University in New York.

His entrepreneurial journey began early, achieving his first million dollars by the age of 26 in 1979 through trading lace and distributing soft drinks. A pivotal moment came in 1991 when his company, Consolidated Oil, discovered oil in commercial quantities in the shallow waters off Southwestern Ondo State, marking the first time an indigenous Nigerian company had achieved this. 

Adenuga’s entry into the telecommunications sector involved navigating regulatory hurdles. Initially granted a GSM license in 1999, it was later revoked, but he successfully re-acquired one during a subsequent government auction in 2003. This led to the establishment of Globacom as a major player in the Nigerian telecom market. His success in the industry was recognized in 2007 when he was named African Entrepreneur of the Year at the African Telecoms Awards. In 2015, he attempted to expand his telecom interests further with a $600 million bid to purchase Comium Côte d'Ivoire, a mobile operator in Ivory Coast.

Adenuga has received numerous honors acknowledging his contributions to business and society. In 2012, the Nigerian government conferred upon him the title of Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger. He also holds the Yoruba chieftaincy title of “Otunba Apesin” within the Ijebu clan. Further international recognition came in 2018 when President Emmanuel Macron of France decorated him with the insignia of a Commander of the Legion of Honour. In 2019, *New African* magazine included him in its list of the Top 100 most influential Africans.

title: Valerie Harper
text:
Valerie Harper, born August 22, 1939, in Suffern, New York, was a celebrated American actress whose career spanned Broadway, television, and film. She began her performing journey as a dancer, debuting on Broadway in *Li'l Abner* and continuing with roles in productions like *Wildcat* and *Take Me Along*. Her early film work included small parts in *Rock, Rock, Rock!* and the film adaptation of *Li’l Abner*.

Harper achieved widespread recognition for her portrayal of Rhoda Morgenstern, initially on *The Mary Tyler Moore Show* from 1970 to 1974, and then as the star of her own spinoff series, *Rhoda*, which ran from 1974 to 1978. This role earned her four Emmy Awards, including one for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series, as well as a Golden Globe Award. She received further Golden Globe nominations for her performances in the films *Freebie and the Bean* (1974) and *Chapter Two* (1979). 

Her television career continued with the sitcom *Valerie* (1986-1987), but she was controversially fired after two seasons following a salary dispute. The show continued as *Valerie’s Family* and then *The Hogan Family*, with her character written out. She successfully sued the production company, Lorimar, and was awarded $1.4 million plus a percentage of the show’s profits.

Later in her career, Harper returned to the stage, earning a Tony Award nomination in 2010 for her performance as Tallulah Bankhead in *Looped*. She also toured with the play *Golda’s Balcony*, portraying Golda Meir, and made guest appearances on television shows like *Touched by an Angel*, *Sex and the City*, and *Desperate Housewives*. In 2013, she appeared as a contestant on *Dancing with the Stars*.

Harper's personal life included a marriage to Richard Schaal from 1964 to 1978, and a later marriage to Tony Cacciotti in 1987, with whom she adopted a daughter, Cristina. She was actively involved in the women’s liberation movement and co-founded the charity L.I.F.E. (Love Is Feeding Everyone) with Dennis Weaver.

In 2009, Harper was diagnosed with lung cancer, and in 2013, she revealed she had leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. Despite this prognosis, she continued to work and fight the disease for several years. She died on August 30, 2019, in Los Angeles, and is buried at Hollywood Forever Cemetery. Before her death, she famously participated in a pact with magician and mentalist Oz Pearlman, revealing a secret code word to be used after her death to test the validity of psychic claims.

title: Jean-Claude Van Damme
text:
Jean-Claude Van Damme, born Jean-Claude Camille François Van Varenberg in 1960 in Brussels, Belgium, rose to international fame as a martial artist and action film star. From a young age, his father enrolled him in karate, leading him to achieve a 2nd-dan black belt and success in competitions, including winning the European Professional Karate Association middleweight championship in 1979 and the Mr. Belgium bodybuilding title in 1978. Driven by a desire to act in Hollywood, he moved to the United States in 1982, taking on various jobs while pursuing his goal, including work as an extra, a bouncer, and a limousine driver.

His breakthrough came with the lead role in *Bloodsport* (1988), a martial arts film that became a box office hit. This launched a string of commercially successful action films throughout the late 1980s and early 1990s, including *Cyborg*, *Kickboxer* (both 1989), *Lionheart*, *Death Warrant* (both 1990), *Double Impact* (1991), and *Universal Soldier* (1992). He achieved “sex symbol” status during this period. He collaborated with several Hong Kong filmmakers—John Woo, Tsui Hark, and Ringo Lam—who made their Western cinema debuts working with him between 1993 and 1998. Films like *Hard Target* (1993) and *Street Fighter* (1994) further cemented his stardom. 

After a decline in popularity in the late 1990s and early 2000s, Van Damme experienced a career resurgence with *JCVD* (2008), a critically acclaimed film in which he played a fictionalized version of himself. He regained prominence in the action genre with a villainous role in *The Expendables 2* (2012), alongside Sylvester Stallone. He continued to appear in action films such as *Enemies Closer* (2013), *Kickboxer: Retaliation* (2018), and *Darkness of Man* (2024), alongside voice work in animated films like *Minions: The Rise of Gru* (2022). He also starred in the television series *Jean-Claude Van Johnson* (2016–2017), produced by Ridley Scott.

Throughout his career, Van Damme’s films have collectively grossed over $3.3 billion worldwide, establishing him as a highly successful action star.  Before his Hollywood success, he competed extensively in karate and kickboxing, compiling a record of 44 wins and 4 losses. He even had a short, though memorable, stint as an early version of the Predator in the 1987 film of the same name before being replaced.  He opened a gym in Brussels called California Gym in 1979 to help finance his move to America. Beyond his film career, Van Damme has been a vocal advocate for conservation and animal rights causes.

title: Grayston Burgess
text:
Grayston Burgess, born in Cheriton, Kent on April 7, 1932, and passing away on March 6, 2019, was a noted English countertenor and conductor. His musical journey began early in life as a chorister at Canterbury Cathedral during the Second World War. He continued his musical education at Cheltenham College, ultimately earning a choral scholarship to King’s College, Cambridge, where he sang under the direction of Boris Ord. 

Burgess’s professional career encompassed both performance and ensemble leadership. He was a member of the Purcell Singers and notably founded the Purcell Consort of Voices in 1963, a group with which he would later record. He also collaborated with international ensembles, performing with the Studio der frühen Musik and the Musica Reservata Ensemble, led by Michael Morrow and John Beckett. As a countertenor soloist, he was involved in premiering new works, including Michael Tippett’s “Songs for Ariel”. His work as a performer is documented in recordings such as a Dowland LP featuring him as a soloist. 

Later in life, Burgess relocated to rural Herefordshire in the 1980s and transitioned towards teaching. He initially taught singing at Ellerslie School in Malvern, and after its closure, continued his teaching at Malvern College. Among his students was Wendy Nieper, a former member of the Swingle Singers.

Even after a long and distinguished career, Burgess remained actively involved in music. In 2000, he accepted an invitation to establish and direct a community choir to commemorate the new millennium. This initial project evolved into Choir 2000, becoming a lasting musical presence in the area and a source of both inspiration and fulfillment for Burgess himself. 

In 2017, the Daily Telegraph recognized him as a ‘veteran conductor and choir director’ in an article concerning women's roles in British cathedral choirs, published on International Women's Day. Interestingly, the article did not acknowledge his connection, if any, to the Campaign for the Traditional Cathedral Choir, a group known for its opposition to the inclusion of women and girls in cathedral and church choirs. Burgess’s conducting work is represented in recordings such as "Music of Albert: Prince of Saxe, Coburg und Gotha" with the Purcell Consort of Voices.

title: Settimo Mineo
text:
Settimo Mineo, born in Palermo on November 28, 1938, is a prominent figure in the Sicilian Mafia, specifically within the Pagliarelli mandamento. Often referred to as “Tonton Settimo,” he is considered one of the oldest current bosses in the organization. While officially operating a jewelry shop in Palermo, his true influence lies within the criminal underworld. 

Mineo’s life has been marked by violence and involvement in Mafia conflicts. He survived an assassination attempt in 1982 that resulted in the death of his brother, Giuseppe, and his brother Antonino was murdered in 1981. His initial involvement with the Mafia brought him to the attention of *pentito* (informant) Tommaso Buscetta, whose testimony led to Mineo’s conviction and a five-year prison sentence during the Maxi Trial. He was again arrested in 2006 and convicted in the “Gotha” trial, but was released in 2013 following a decision by the Supreme Court of Cassation.

Throughout his career, Mineo has demonstrated a shifting allegiance within the complex power structures of the Cosa Nostra. He was formerly associated with Antonio Rotolo and the Corleonesi clan, but later forged alliances with rivals of both—Franco and Tommaso Inzerillo of the Inzerillo clan—and counted Salvatore Sorrentino as a close associate. This shift indicates a deliberate change in sides within the Mafia’s internal dynamics.

In a significant development, Mineo was elected as the new head of the Sicilian Mafia Commission in May 2018, following the death of Salvatore Riina. However, this position was short-lived, as he was re-arrested in December 2018 during the “Cupola 2.0” operation conducted by the Carabinieri, charged with leading the “Dome” of Cosa Nostra. After his most recent arrest, Giuseppe Calvaruso, previously Mineo’s most trusted lieutenant, assumed leadership of the Pagliarelli mandamento. Calvaruso is noted for his modern approach to managing the mandamento’s criminal activities, demonstrating a more entrepreneurial attitude.

Prior to his arrests, Mineo was known for his personal charisma and ability to mediate conflicts. Notably, he eschewed modern technology, refusing to use mobile phones for fear of surveillance, and frequently travelled on foot, even when meeting with other Mafia leaders. Despite his criminal lifestyle, Mineo and his wife were actively involved in their local community, regularly attending mass at the Church of San Giovanni Decollato in Ballarò, Palermo, and participating in a year-long volunteer program supporting an after-school program for children at the church.

title: Sandra Pisani
text:
Sandra Pisani, born in Adelaide, South Australia on January 23, 1959, was a highly accomplished Australian field hockey player and contributor to the sport who sadly passed away on April 19, 2022, after a battle with cancer. She represented Australia in 85 international matches, serving as captain of the national team from 1985 to 1987. Her playing career culminated in a gold medal at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, a historic achievement as it marked Australia’s first Olympic gold in women’s field hockey.
